questions.question: A water utility is designing an assistant to triage inbound leak reports. The team has moved straight to debating whether to build it as a fixed workflow or an autonomous agent. Before that debate can be settled, what has to happen?

options.A: Prototype both patterns against a sample of historical leak reports and adopt whichever scores better
options.B: Split the work into three buckets — what Claude handles, what existing systems handle, and what people handle — so the pattern is chosen against a defined scope
options.C: Adopt the agent pattern, since it can accommodate whichever steps turn out to be required
options.D: Write the system prompt first, since it determines what the assistant is able to do

rationale.correct: Decomposition comes before architecture. Until the work is split into three buckets — what Claude handles, what the existing systems handle, and what a person handles — there is no defined scope for a pattern to cover, and the split is driven by how the model actually behaves on each piece. Skipping it is how deterministic work ends up inside the model and how the assistant ends up operating without context a colleague would have been given.

distractors.A: Prototyping compares two patterns against an undefined scope. Whichever prototype wins, the design still contains whatever work was never consciously allocated, and the comparison cannot surface that.
distractors.C: Choosing the most permissive pattern to avoid making the allocation is the decomposition failure in its most expensive form: the agent absorbs the deterministic and human-judgement work along with everything else.
distractors.D: The system prompt is downstream of the split. Written first, it necessarily encodes an allocation nobody has examined.

questions.question: An insurer's assistant calculates premium adjustments by reasoning over rate tables supplied in its context. Most adjustments are correct, but a small proportion are arithmetically wrong, and the same input does not reliably reproduce the same error. What is the underlying design fault?

options.A: The rate tables sit in the middle of the prompt and should be moved to a boundary where attention is stronger
options.B: Deterministic calculation was allocated to the wrong bucket: a rating engine should compute the adjustment and the model should call it, rather than the model being made to perform the arithmetic
options.C: Sampling is introducing variation and the temperature should be reduced to zero so the arithmetic becomes repeatable
options.D: The workload has outgrown the model tier and a more capable model should be adopted, since arithmetic reliability improves with capability

rationale.correct: This is forcing Claude into system logic. Of the three buckets, arithmetic against a rate table belongs squarely in the one existing systems own: a rating engine performs it exactly and repeatably. The tell is non-reproducibility: a rating engine given the same inputs cannot produce a different answer, and a probabilistic system given the same inputs can. Moving the calculation behind a tool call removes the error class entirely rather than reducing its frequency.

distractors.A: Prompt positioning changes how reliably instructions are followed, not whether a probabilistic process should have been performing exact arithmetic in the first place. It would move the error rate without removing the error class.
distractors.C: Reducing sampling randomness makes a wrong answer more consistent, not more correct. It also removes the variability that is currently the clearest evidence of where the work has been misplaced.
distractors.D: A more capable model computes more of these correctly and still offers no guarantee. Paying more per request to reduce, but not eliminate, an error class that a rating engine eliminates outright is the wrong trade.

questions.question: For each scenario, identify the most appropriate architectural pattern. Options may be used more than once.

scenarios.text: Converting each inbound request-for-quote email into a structured record, with the customer's existing contract terms retrieved as context.
A quarterly regulatory filing assembled the same way every time: extract, reconcile, validate, format, submit.
Tracing the cause of a batch of failed overnight settlements, where each query result determines what is worth examining next.
A site acquisition review requiring planning, environmental and structural assessments, each needing its own tools and specialist context, combined into a single recommendation.
Rewriting each supplier notice into plain language against a controlled glossary of approved terms.

rationale.correct: These four patterns are points on the autonomy spectrum, running from the model assisting with one step to the model planning the whole sequence. The first and last scenarios are single transformations with the necessary context supplied alongside them, which is one augmented LLM call each — retrieval or a glossary in the prompt does not make a task agentic. The quarterly filing is a stable sequence whose steps are known in advance and identical every time, which is the definition of a fixed workflow. The settlement investigation cannot be enumerated in advance because each query result determines the next, which is what an autonomous plan-act-observe loop exists for. The site acquisition review needs genuinely different specialisations, each with its own tools and context, coordinated into one output, which is what justifies multi-agent coordination overhead.

questions.question: A pharmaceutical manufacturer is choosing between a fixed workflow and an autonomous agent for batch-release documentation review. Assessing the five factors: predictability is high, latency tolerance is generous, cost is unconstrained, and observability is good — but a missed deviation reaching release is a reportable regulatory event. Which line of reasoning is correct?

options.A: Four of the five factors permit an agent, so the agent is indicated and the remaining factor is managed operationally
options.B: Error cost is the tightest constraint, and the tightest constraint is the factor that decides — it selects the workflow however permissive the other four are
options.C: Latency tolerance is generous, so the agent's additional reasoning steps are affordable here and the agent should be preferred
options.D: Run both patterns in parallel for a quarter and adopt whichever produces fewer missed deviations

rationale.correct: The five factors are not scored and totalled. The framework is that the tightest constraint is the factor that decides, and when error cost is that constraint, error cost picks the pattern. A reportable regulatory event is exactly the case where a wrong answer is expensive enough to override how permissive everything else looks, so the pattern must be the one whose steps are defined in advance and individually auditable.

distractors.A: Counting permissive factors inverts the framework. The binding constraint is decisive precisely because the others are slack, so the fact that four are permissive is the reason the fifth governs, not a reason to discount it.
distractors.C: Latency tolerance is genuinely generous here, which is why it is not the deciding factor. Choosing a pattern on a slack constraint means the tight one goes unaddressed.
distractors.D: Running an unsuitable pattern against live batch release to find out how often it misses a deviation treats the regulatory event as an acceptable experimental cost. The framework exists so that this is decided before exposure, not measured through it.

questions.question: An airline built its line-maintenance assistant as an autonomous agent that plans its own diagnostic sequence and can raise parts orders below a value threshold. After two events requiring investigation, the review finds the agent had taken defensible but non-standard diagnostic paths that engineers could not afterwards reconstruct. What does this finding indicate?

options.A: The standard diagnostic sequence should be written into the system prompt so the agent follows it
options.B: Autonomy was granted beyond what the error cost tolerates — over-granting agentic autonomy — and a pattern with defined steps would have kept each path reconstructable
options.C: The pattern is sound and the gap is evidential: session logging should be extended so paths can be reconstructed after future events
options.D: The model tier is the constraint, and a more capable model would select more conventional diagnostic paths

rationale.correct: Autonomy is granted, not assumed, and how much of it is affordable is set by the error cost. In line maintenance a wrong or unexplainable diagnostic path is expensive enough that the sequence has to be defined in advance and individually auditable, which is a workflow rather than an agent. The symptom is diagnostic: paths that were defensible yet unreconstructable is what over-granting agentic autonomy looks like after the fact.

distractors.A: Putting the sequence in the prompt asks an instruction to do an architecture's job. The agent still plans its own path and may still depart from the documented one, so nothing is guaranteed — only requested.
distractors.C: Better logging would let the airline reconstruct the next non-standard path rather than prevent it. That is a detective control applied where the requirement is that the path be constrained in the first place.
distractors.D: A more capable model is likely to choose conventional paths more often, which lowers the frequency of the finding without changing the property the review actually objected to.

questions.question: A food producer is deciding whether its allergen-labelling checks should run as a fixed workflow. Which TWO characteristics of the problem most strongly indicate that pattern? (Select TWO)

options.A: Each step must be individually auditable and reproducible for the food safety authority
options.B: The team wants the system to recover on its own when a tool call fails mid-check
options.C: The processing steps are known in advance and are the same for every product record
options.D: The volume of product records to be checked is expected to grow substantially
options.E: Reducing the number of model calls per record is the primary objective

rationale.correct: A fixed workflow is warranted on two conditions, and both hold here. The steps are known in advance and identical for every request, so there is nothing for a planner to decide at run time. And each step must be individually auditable and reproducible, which a sequence of discrete calls gives directly and a planned path does not — a regulator asking why a particular record passed needs the same answer every time it asks.

distractors.B: Autonomous recovery from an unexpected failure is the capability that distinguishes an agent from a workflow. Wanting it is an argument for the other pattern, not this one.
distractors.D: Growing volume is a scaling concern and is addressed within whichever pattern is chosen. It does not favour one over the other.
distractors.E: Call count is a cost characteristic. A workflow often uses more calls than a single prompt, so optimising for fewer calls would argue against the pattern the other conditions clearly indicate.

questions.question: A regional electricity distributor is building a customer assistant to answer questions such as how much a customer currently owes, whether their address is affected by an outage, and when restoration is estimated. The team proposes indexing a nightly export of account balances and outage records into a vector store and answering from retrieval. At design review an architect objects. What is the strongest basis for the objection?

options.A: Vector stores cannot represent numeric fields such as balances with sufficient precision
options.B: The data is live state rather than reference material, so it must be read through a tool call against the system of record at request time and not served from a periodic export
options.C: A nightly export is too infrequent for this use case and should be rebuilt hourly so answers stay acceptably fresh
options.D: Retrieval is workable provided the assistant discloses that figures may be up to a day old

rationale.correct: Retrieval is built for static documents and stale snapshots, and using it as a substitute for live state is the most common architectural mistake in this family. Balances, outage status and restoration estimates are transactional state owned by a system of record, so the only way an answer is correct at the moment it is given is to read that state when the question is asked. Any export-based design is wrong by an interval, and here the interval is the whole question.

distractors.A: Numeric values can be stored and returned faithfully from an index. The defect is the age of the snapshot, not the fidelity of the representation.
distractors.C: Shortening the interval shrinks the window of wrongness without closing it. A restoration estimate can change minutes after any export, and the customers most likely to ask are precisely those whose state has just changed.
distractors.D: This is accurate disclosure of a defect rather than a remedy. It transfers the cost of a stale architecture onto the customer at the moment they most need a reliable answer.

questions.question: A hotel group wants an assistant that answers guest questions about facilities, house policies, opening times and seasonal offers across its properties. That content is documentary and is edited by property managers most days. Which approach fits?

options.A: Fine-tune a model on the current content and repeat the exercise each quarter
options.B: Augment the model with retrieval over the live content repository so answers reflect the current documents
options.C: Place every property's document set in the context window on each request so nothing can be missed
options.D: Rely on the base model's general knowledge of hotel operations and note that details vary between properties

rationale.correct: This content is genuinely documentary — it is written, edited and read as reference material — which makes retrieval augmentation the right pattern even though it changes daily. The distinction that matters is not how often something changes but what kind of thing it is: reference material is retrieved, transactional state is read from its system of record. Here the assistant answers from the current documents without retraining and without carrying every property's content on every request.

distractors.A: Retraining on a quarterly cycle bakes in a snapshot that is wrong within days, and it pays a large fixed cost to achieve what retrieval achieves continuously.
distractors.C: Loading every property's documents on every request pays for the whole estate to answer a question about one property, and the context cost grows with each property added.
distractors.D: General knowledge of how hotels work cannot answer a question about this group's policies, and the caveat does not make the answer usable — it only warns the guest that it might not be.

questions.question: A law firm's matter-intake system has two distinct weaknesses. Matters are sometimes directed to the wrong practice group in ways only a specialist notices, and extraction of key dates from client documents fails on unfamiliar layouts. The team is debating whether to adopt the Routing architecture or the evaluator-optimiser document pipeline. What is the strongest recommendation?

options.A: Adopt Routing alone, since misdirection happens first and correcting it will reduce the downstream extraction failures
options.B: Adopt both, because the two parts of the system break differently — route the matter to its practice group, and run extraction through an evaluator-optimiser loop that checks its own output
options.C: Adopt neither and design a bespoke architecture matched exactly to this firm's intake process
options.D: Adopt whichever of the two the team has more experience operating, and revisit the decision once the system has run for two quarters

rationale.correct: Reference architectures are combined when different parts of a system break differently, and that is exactly the finding here: one failure is a classification problem and the other is an extraction-quality problem. Routing addresses the first, an evaluator-optimiser loop addresses the second by checking output against the source before accepting it, and neither one addresses the other. Reaching for the tested architectures also means the failure modes of each are already documented.

distractors.A: Sending the matter to the right practice group does not make an unfamiliar document layout easier to extract from. The two failures are independent, so fixing one leaves the other at its current rate.
distractors.C: A bespoke design forfeits what the documented architectures already encode about how each one fails, and this firm's intake process is not unusual enough to justify learning those lessons again.
distractors.D: Operational familiarity is a real consideration when architectures are otherwise equivalent. Here they are not equivalent — each addresses a different one of the two known defects — so familiarity selects which defect goes unfixed.

questions.question: A shipping group is assessing whether its vessel-chartering review justifies a multi-agent design rather than one augmented agent. Which TWO characteristics of the task most strongly indicate that multiple agents are warranted? (Select TWO)

options.A: Distinct sub-tasks require different specialisation, tools and context that would overload a single agent
options.B: The number of charter reviews the group handles is expected to rise sharply
options.C: Several sub-tasks are independent and can run in parallel to shorten the end-to-end review
options.D: The review currently occupies three analysts for a week and the cost of that is well understood
options.E: The board has asked for the most advanced architecture available to it

rationale.correct: Multi-agent designs carry real coordination overhead, so they earn it on two conditions. Sub-tasks must need genuinely different specialisation, tools and context — enough that loading them into one agent would degrade it — and independent sub-tasks must be able to run in parallel so the structure buys back end-to-end time. Both hold for a chartering review that spans commercial, technical and legal assessment.

distractors.B: Rising volume is addressed by scaling whichever pattern is chosen. It says nothing about whether the work needs to be divided across specialists.
distractors.D: Knowing what the manual process costs establishes that automating it is worth something. It does not indicate how the automated version should be structured.
distractors.E: Architectural sophistication is not a requirement, and treating it as one produces coordination overhead the problem has not asked for.

questions.question: A mining operator's permit-compliance pipeline uses four specialists: sampling intake, assay validation, threshold screening, and disclosure drafting. The regulator requires a complete record of every determination in the order it was made, and drafting must not run at all if screening flags an exceedance. Which orchestration strategy satisfies both requirements?

options.A: Peer-to-peer handoffs in which each specialist decides which specialist to invoke next
options.B: A supervisor that invokes each specialist in sequence, records each outcome as it happens, and halts the chain on an exceedance
options.C: All four specialists run in parallel and their outputs are merged once the slowest completes
options.D: A single agent holding all four specialists' tools, instructed to work through them in the required order and to stop on an exceedance

rationale.correct: A supervisor gives all three of the properties the regulator is asking for: central sequencing, a single place where each outcome is recorded as an ordered audit trail, and one point of control that halts the chain when screening flags an exceedance. Both requirements are guarantees rather than tendencies, and a supervisor is what makes them structural.

distractors.A: With each specialist choosing its successor, both the order of execution and the decision to stop become emergent properties. They will usually be right, and a regulator is asking for a guarantee rather than a tendency.
distractors.C: Running everything at once minimises elapsed time and directly violates the stated requirement, because drafting has already executed by the time screening's flag is known.
distractors.D: Here the ordering and the stop condition are carried by an instruction rather than by the architecture. The agent may comply on most runs, but nothing prevents a departure and nothing records the sequence as an obligation.

questions.question: A construction consultancy asks Claude, in a single prompt, to read a long tender document, assess it against every one of the firm's internal bid criteria, score the opportunity and draft a bid or no-bid note. Output quality is uneven: some criteria are skipped without comment and the scoring reasoning is thin. The prompt wording has already been reworked twice. What is the most effective next step?

options.A: Move to the largest available model and raise the maximum output tokens so there is room to cover everything
options.B: Decompose the task into sequenced subtasks — extract, assess each criteria group, score, then synthesise — passing structured output between steps
options.C: Add worked examples of well-written bid and no-bid notes so the model has a clearer target
options.D: Lower the temperature so the instructions are followed more literally

rationale.correct: The failure signature — items silently skipped and reasoning that thins out across a long multi-part task — is a decomposition problem rather than a wording problem, which is why two rewrites changed nothing. Sequenced subtasks give each step focused context and a verifiable intermediate output, so a skipped criteria group becomes visible as a missing structured result rather than an absence nobody notices. Passing structured output between steps is what converts silent omission into a detectable one.

distractors.A: This treats capacity as the constraint when structure is. A larger model with more room to write will cover more criteria on average and still has no mechanism that makes an omission visible.
distractors.C: Examples raise the quality of the parts the model already attempts. They do not cause it to attempt the parts it is currently skipping, because the gap is coverage rather than craft.
distractors.D: Sampling randomness is not why criteria are being missed. A more deterministic run reproduces the same omissions more consistently.

questions.question: A university's student-services agent covers admissions, timetabling, fees and accommodation. Its tool count and system prompt have grown with each area added, and tool-selection accuracy has fallen steadily over the same period. Faculty now want library services added as a fifth area. What is the strongest architectural recommendation?

options.A: Add the library tools now and schedule a prompt rewrite for the following term
options.B: Split the agent into domain-specific agents behind a router, each with a focused toolset and prompt, so library services becomes an addition rather than a further burden
options.C: Expand the system prompt so each area is described in more detail and the boundaries between them are clearer
options.D: Require a tool call on every request so the agent stops answering from general knowledge

rationale.correct: Tool-selection accuracy declining as breadth grows is the classic signal of a single agent carrying more than it can hold. A router in front of domain-specific agents restores a focused toolset and prompt for each area, and it changes the economics of expansion: a fifth area becomes another agent behind the router rather than more weight on one. The current design makes every addition worse for every existing area.

distractors.A: Adding a fifth area to an agent already degrading under four compounds the problem, and defers the fix to a point where there is more to unpick.
distractors.C: More detail means more prompt, and prompt length is part of what is degrading selection. This makes the instructions harder to follow rather than easier.
distractors.D: Forcing a tool call addresses a different failure — answering from general knowledge instead of the tools — which is not what the evidence describes. Choosing wrongly from too many tools is not fixed by choosing more often.

questions.question: An international NGO has collected candidate use cases from every department and asks its architect which should be built first. Which TWO considerations should most strongly drive that selection? (Select TWO)

options.A: Measurable business value — a cost, cycle-time or service-level improvement that can be stated as a number
options.B: Feasible access to the data the use case needs, with risk that can be managed at the NGO's current maturity
options.C: The department whose staff are most enthusiastic, since willing users make adoption more likely
options.D: The use case covering the largest volume of work, since scale multiplies whatever benefit is achieved
options.E: Piloting all of the candidates so the strongest emerges from evidence rather than argument

rationale.correct: A first use case is selected on measurable value balanced against feasibility and risk, because those two together determine whether the project can both succeed and be seen to have succeeded. Value that can be stated as a number is what sustains funding for the second project, and feasible data access with manageable risk is what determines whether the first one ships at all. Either alone selects badly: valuable but infeasible stalls, feasible but marginal proves nothing.

distractors.C: Enthusiasm genuinely helps adoption, and it is a tie-breaker rather than a driver. Selecting on it alone optimises for internal politics and can land on a use case with no demonstrable benefit.
distractors.D: Volume multiplies benefit only once there is benefit per unit to multiply. A large volume of low-value work produces a large project with a small result.
distractors.E: Piloting everything spends the effort of the first project several times over before any of it ships, which is the opposite of what a first use case is for.

questions.question: A veterinary group's case-triage classifier has been in production for five months. Dashboards cover latency and cost, and clinicians quietly correct a proportion of its classifications in the practice management system. Nobody can currently say whether the classifications are right. Which architectural addition most directly closes that gap?

options.A: An alert that fires when daily token spend departs from its established norm
options.B: A feedback loop that captures the clinician corrections already being made and routes a sample of production classifications into a labelled evaluation set
options.C: A larger model, on the basis that classification accuracy rises with model capability
options.D: A monthly review of the system prompt to confirm the triage instructions are still current

rationale.correct: The missing element is the feedback stage: production correctness signals flowing back into something evaluable. The clinician corrections are already being generated as a by-product of normal work and are simply not being captured, so the cheapest available ground truth is currently discarded daily. Routing those corrections plus a sample of live classifications into a labelled evaluation set turns an unanswerable question into a measured one.

distractors.A: Token spend is a cost signal. It moves when usage patterns change and stays flat while classifications quietly become wrong, so it cannot answer the question being asked.
distractors.C: Changing the model without a way to measure correctness means the group would not be able to tell whether the change helped, which leaves it in exactly the position it is trying to escape.
distractors.D: Reviewing the prompt confirms the configuration matches intent. It says nothing about whether the output matches reality, which is the gap.

questions.question: A telecoms operator is starting its first production workload: summarising network incident reports for an operations dashboard. No evaluation set exists yet. Two engineers argue for the most capable tier to be safe, another for the cheapest on the grounds that summarising is undemanding. What is the defensible starting position?

options.A: Begin on the most capable tier and step down later if cost becomes a problem
options.B: Begin on Sonnet as the default tier, and treat any later move up or down as a release requiring an evaluation set and a rollback criterion
options.C: Begin on the cheapest tier, since summarising is among the least demanding things the platform will be asked to do
options.D: Defer the model decision until an evaluation set exists, and prototype without committing to a tier

rationale.correct: Sonnet is the default tier because it balances intelligence, speed and cost across most production workloads, which makes it the position that needs the least justification when nothing has been measured yet. It also sets up the discipline that follows: once there is an evaluation set, moving up or down becomes a deliberate, gated change rather than a preference. Starting anywhere else means the first tier decision is made on argument rather than evidence and then quietly inherited.

distractors.A: Starting at the top and descending sounds cautious, but it establishes a cost base the operator then has to argue its way down from, usually without the evaluation set that would make the descent safe.
distractors.C: Summarising incident reports faithfully, without dropping the detail an engineer needs, is not obviously undemanding. This substitutes an impression of task difficulty for a measurement of it.
distractors.D: Prototyping without a tier is not possible, so in practice this means someone picks one informally and the decision is made without being examined.

questions.question: A retail analytics team runs product classification on Sonnet. Volume has grown and finance has asked whether a smaller tier would serve. An engineer ran a hundred hand-picked examples through both and reports that the outputs look equivalent. The team proposes switching next sprint and watching the support queue for a fortnight, reverting if ticket volume climbs. What must be established before the swap proceeds?

options.A: A published third-party benchmark comparing the two tiers on general reasoning
options.B: An eval set defining what better means for this workload, and a rollback criterion agreed before the swap rather than inferred from what happens afterwards
options.C: Nothing further, because watching the support queue after a staged release is itself the rollback mechanism
options.D: A commitment to stay on the current tier, since the more capable option is the safer default for anything in production

rationale.correct: Every model swap is a release and gets the gate any release gets, and that gate has two halves. There must be an eval set that defines what better means against this workload's own labelled cases, and there must be a rollback criterion fixed in advance so the decision to revert is measured against a threshold rather than argued about under pressure a fortnight later. A hundred hand-picked examples and an impression of equivalence is neither of those things.

distractors.A: A benchmark measures the model, not the workload. Parity on general reasoning implies nothing about classification accuracy over this particular catalogue of products.
distractors.C: A staged release is a legitimate mechanism, but here it is being asked to do the evaluation's job as well. Support tickets are a lagging and noisy proxy, and with no threshold set in advance, ticket volume climbing is a judgement call rather than a trigger.
distractors.D: Refusing to evaluate forfeits a real cost saving on the assumption that quality would suffer, which is the same substitution of argument for evidence the proposal itself makes, pointed the other way.

questions.question: A publisher classifies a very large daily volume of reader comments into moderation categories. On a labelled test set, accuracy sits within a point across the whole model family. The business is sensitive to both latency and cost. Which model strategy is most defensible?

options.A: Use the most capable model, since a moderation error costs more than the compute ever will
options.B: Use the smallest model that meets the accuracy target, and keep validating that it still meets it with ongoing evaluation
options.C: Use the mid-tier model as a compromise, which avoids having to repeat this comparison
options.D: Alternate between tiers by time of day so that peak-hour latency improves

rationale.correct: When accuracy is comparable across the family, capability has stopped being the differentiator and latency and cost start deciding. At this volume the disciplined choice is the smallest model that meets the target, with ongoing evaluation confirming it continues to meet it as the comment distribution shifts. The evaluation is the part that makes the choice defensible rather than merely cheap.

distractors.A: The premise may well be true and it is not what the measurement says. Accuracy is within a point across the family, so the more expensive tier is not buying the error reduction this argument assumes.
distractors.C: Splitting the difference avoids the decision rather than making it, and it forgoes the evaluation that would have told the publisher which tier was actually required.
distractors.D: Behaviour that varies with the clock is difficult to debug and difficult to explain to a moderator disputing a decision, and it delivers the latency improvement only during the hours it is least likely to be scrutinised.

questions.question: A bank's operations assistant loads its full policy manual, its full product reference and the customer's entire interaction history into context on every request. It performs well today. The roadmap adds two product lines and a regulatory annex over the next year. What should the architect flag now?

options.A: Nothing yet — the design performs well, and it should be revisited when a request actually fails
options.B: This is monolithic context, which grows until it breaks; moving to progressive context, where each step receives only what it needs, is what holds up across a long-lived deployment
options.C: The context budget will need to be raised in step with each addition to the roadmap
options.D: The policy manual should be condensed so that the new product lines fit alongside it

rationale.correct: Loading everything up front is monolithic context, and its defining property is that it works right up until it does not. Progressive context, where the model receives only what it needs at each step, is what holds up over a long-lived deployment, because each addition to the roadmap then costs only the requests that actually need it. The moment to change is while the design still works, since afterwards the change is made under pressure.

distractors.A: Waiting for a failure means the redesign happens after the deployment has been extended twice, when the coupling is deeper and the change is more expensive.
distractors.C: Raising the budget each time a product line is added treats the symptom on a schedule set by the roadmap, and every request continues to pay for material it does not use.
distractors.D: Condensing the manual buys one round of headroom at the cost of the detail that made the answers trustworthy, and the next two additions consume it.

questions.question: An online gaming platform places a request identifier and the current timestamp at the very top of its system prompt, followed by a large block of static moderation policy, then the player's message. Prompt caching is enabled but the hit rate is effectively zero. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The static policy block is too large to be eligible for caching
options.B: The dynamic values sit at the start, so the prefix differs on every request and no cached prefix can ever match
options.C: The moderation policy should sit in the player's message rather than the system prompt, so it caches alongside the turn
options.D: The hit rate is measuring cache writes rather than reads, and the cache is in fact working normally

rationale.correct: Prompt caching matches on the prefix, so what matters is not how much static content there is but how early the first variable byte appears. An identifier and a timestamp at position zero make every prefix unique, and nothing after them can ever be reused however stable it is. Moving the dynamic values after the static block restores cacheability without changing what the model is told.

distractors.A: Size is not what disqualifies this content. A large stable block is exactly what caching exists to help with, which is why the current ordering is such an expensive mistake.
distractors.C: Relocating the policy moves the same tokens to a different field without making any of them reusable, because the varying values would still precede them in the assembled prompt.
distractors.D: This explains away the measurement rather than the design. A hit rate of effectively zero across sustained traffic is the expected reading for a prefix that changes on every request, so the metric is describing the system accurately.

questions.question: A recruitment platform applied chain-of-thought prompting uniformly across its features. It improved a complex candidate-shortlisting feature. A simple endpoint that extracts dates and job titles from a CV is now slower and more expensive with no measurable change in accuracy. What should the architect conclude?

options.A: Chain-of-thought should be withdrawn across the platform, since it roughly doubles token use wherever it is applied
options.B: Chain-of-thought earns its tokens on multi-step reasoning and adds cost and latency without benefit on simple extraction, so it should be applied selectively per task on measured benefit
options.C: The extraction endpoint needs a longer and more explicit chain-of-thought prompt before the benefit becomes visible
options.D: Chain-of-thought only produces gains on the most capable tier, and the extraction endpoint runs on a smaller one

rationale.correct: The evidence contains both results, and a conclusion has to account for both. Chain-of-thought earns its tokens where there are genuine intermediate steps, and buys nothing where the task is to locate a field and return it. That makes it a per-task technique applied selectively on measured benefit, which is the same discipline any other optimisation gets.

distractors.A: Withdrawing it platform-wide discards a measured improvement on the shortlisting feature to fix a measured regression on the extraction endpoint. It treats a per-task result as a platform-wide verdict.
distractors.C: This doubles down where the measurement already shows no benefit. Extraction has no intermediate reasoning to elaborate, so a longer reasoning prompt produces more tokens describing a lookup.
distractors.D: The premise is not how the technique behaves. It is also contradicted by the platform's own evidence, since the shortlisting gain was observed on the tier that feature already runs on.

questions.question: A vehicle manufacturer's dealer-support assistant carries a rule that internal margin figures must never be disclosed. It sits in the middle of a large block of product and pricing reference material in the system prompt, and it is followed inconsistently. Rewording it has not helped. Which change is most likely to improve adherence?

options.A: Repeat the rule after every section of the reference material so it cannot be lost
options.B: Move the rule to a boundary of the prompt and separate rules from reference content with clear structure
options.C: Put the rule in capitals so that it registers as higher priority than the surrounding text
options.D: Set the temperature to zero so that the assistant's behaviour becomes deterministic

rationale.correct: A rule buried mid-prompt is competing with reference material for attention at the position where positional attention is weakest, which is why rewording changed nothing — the problem is where it sits rather than what it says. Moving it to a boundary and structurally separating rules from reference content addresses the actual mechanism. Structure is doing the work here, not emphasis.

distractors.A: Repetition adds length to the block that is already crowding the rule out, and it teaches nothing about which content is instruction and which is reference.
distractors.C: Capitalisation is not a priority signal, and adopting it as one tends to spread until several rules are capitalised and the distinction means nothing again.
distractors.D: Temperature governs sampling variation, not which parts of a long prompt the model weights. Behaviour becomes more repeatable without becoming more compliant.

questions.question: An insurance operations team had an extraction endpoint returning inconsistent output shapes. They added twelve few-shot examples, all drawn from motor claims, their highest-volume category. Motor extraction is now near-perfect. Property and liability extraction, previously mediocre but usable, has become noticeably worse, with motor-specific fields being forced onto unrelated documents. What is the most likely explanation?

options.A: Twelve examples exceed what the model can attend to, and reducing the set to three would restore general performance
options.B: The examples are unrepresentative of the task's real input distribution, so they have narrowed behaviour toward the category they demonstrate rather than teaching the general format rule
options.C: The examples belong in the user message rather than the system prompt, where they would be weighted less strongly
options.D: Few-shot prompting is unsuited to structured extraction and should be replaced by lowering the temperature

rationale.correct: Few-shot examples do not merely illustrate a format, they demonstrate what the task is. A set drawn entirely from one category tells the model the task is that category, so it generalises that schema onto documents which do not have it. The remedy is examples spanning the categories in proportion to the real input mix, with the format rule stated explicitly rather than left to be inferred from what the examples happen to share.

distractors.A: There is no such attention threshold at this scale, and cutting the set would preserve the skew while discarding the coverage that made motor extraction reliable.
distractors.C: Relocating the examples changes neither what they demonstrate nor how unrepresentative they are. The defect is in their composition, so it travels with them.
distractors.D: Few-shot is well suited to structured extraction, which is precisely why it fixed the motor case. Sampling temperature does not determine which schema the model believes it has been asked for.

questions.question: An engineering standards assistant places its entire standards collection in the context window on every request. Answers citing material from the middle of the collection are noticeably less reliable, and cost per request is high. Which TWO changes address both problems? (Select TWO)

options.A: Retrieve only the sections relevant to each question and include those instead of the whole collection
options.B: Have the assistant re-read the collection before answering so that material in the middle is reinforced
options.C: Chunk the collection along its structural boundaries so that retrieved sections remain self-contained
options.D: Strip headings and whitespace so the collection consumes fewer tokens
options.E: State in each response when the supporting material came from the middle of the collection so engineers can weigh it accordingly

rationale.correct: Both stated problems have the same root, which is that every request carries the whole collection. Retrieving only the relevant sections sidesteps mid-context recall degradation because the retained material is short enough to be attended to evenly, and it cuts per-request tokens by the ratio of relevant material to total. Structure-aware chunking is what makes that retrieval trustworthy, since a section severed mid-clause is retrieved intact but read without the context that gave it meaning.

distractors.B: Re-reading multiplies the token cost that is already the complaint, and it asks the model to compensate at run time for a structural property of the prompt.
distractors.D: Removing headings and whitespace saves a small fraction of the tokens while destroying the document structure that tells the model where one standard ends and the next begins.
distractors.E: Annotating an unreliable answer as possibly unreliable leaves the engineer to do the verification the assistant was built to do, and it reduces neither the recall problem nor the cost.

questions.question: A logistics platform runs a high volume of requests against a large, mostly static system prompt, and per-request cost is rising faster than usage. Which TWO techniques most directly reduce that cost while preserving capability? (Select TWO)

options.A: Structure the prompt so the static prefix is cacheable, and enable prompt caching
options.B: Raise the maximum output tokens so that fewer follow-up requests are needed
options.C: Load specialised instructions on demand — modular prompts or Skills — rather than including every instruction in every request
options.D: Add more worked examples so that the model succeeds on the first attempt more often
options.E: Move the static content out of the system prompt and into the user message

rationale.correct: These two attack the cost from opposite ends and compose well. A cacheable static prefix means the large stable block is paid for once rather than on every request, and loading specialised instructions on demand means each request carries only the instructions that request actually needs. Together they turn a prompt that grows with the platform's feature count into one that grows with the individual request's requirements.

distractors.B: This trades input cost for output cost and usually increases the total, because longer permitted responses tend to become longer actual responses whether or not the extra length was needed.
distractors.D: More examples means more tokens on every single request, which moves the cost in exactly the wrong direction to buy a success-rate improvement that caching and on-demand loading do not have to pay for.
distractors.E: Relocating the same content between fields changes which part of the request carries it and not how many tokens are billed, and it forfeits the stable prefix that makes caching possible.

questions.question: A pharmacy chain's assistant behaves inconsistently on the same class of question: sometimes it suggests an over-the-counter alternative, sometimes it declines and refers the customer to a pharmacist. The system prompt contains an instruction to be helpful and offer alternatives, and elsewhere an instruction never to advise on substituting a medicine. Which TWO practices most improve adherence? (Select TWO)

options.A: Organise the prompt into clearly delimited sections that state explicit priority where rules conflict
options.B: Raise the temperature so the assistant explores more interpretations and settles on the better one
options.C: Include concrete examples of correct handling for the cases it currently gets wrong
options.D: Place the most critical rules in the middle of the prompt, where attention is strongest
options.E: Remove the section structure so the prompt reads as natural, flowing prose

rationale.correct: The inconsistency is not random, it is a genuine conflict between two instructions that both apply, and the model is resolving it differently on different runs because nothing tells it which one wins. Delimited sections carrying explicit priority remove the ambiguity at its source. Concrete examples of the cases currently handled wrongly then anchor the resolution in the specific situations where the conflict actually arises, which prose alone tends not to settle.

distractors.B: More exploration of an ambiguous instruction set produces more varied resolutions of the same conflict, which is the opposite of what consistency requires.
distractors.D: The middle of a long prompt is where attention is weakest, so this places the rules that matter most in the position they are least likely to be followed from.
distractors.E: Flowing prose removes the delimiters that let the model tell one rule's scope from another's, which makes a conflict between two instructions harder to resolve rather than easier.

questions.question: A payments platform is exposing its internal transactions system through an MCP server so that several teams' Claude-based applications can query it. The system holds per-customer financial records. Which TWO controls must be in place before that server is made available? (Select TWO)

options.A: A system prompt instruction, shared with every consuming team, directing the model to return only records belonging to the requesting customer
options.B: Identity propagated from the calling end user to the server, which authorises every request against that identity rather than against a shared service credential
options.C: A larger context window on consuming applications so a full transaction history can be returned in one call
options.D: A tool surface scoped to least privilege, with state-changing operations such as refunds and reversals excluded or placed behind an explicit approval gate
options.E: Retention of full request and response payloads so access can be reviewed each quarter

rationale.correct: The server is the security boundary, so both controls have to live in it. Propagated end-user identity with server-side authorisation means a consuming application cannot retrieve records it has no right to, whatever the model is persuaded to ask for. Least-privilege scoping with state changes gated means that a request which passes authorisation still cannot move money without a deliberate second step. Together they bound what can be read and what can be done, which are separate questions.

distractors.A: This is a prompt-based auth bypass waiting to be found. An instruction is not an access-control mechanism: it may be ignored, overridden by injected content, or simply not followed, and it leaves the server willing to hand any customer's records to whoever asks convincingly.
distractors.C: Context capacity has no bearing on entitlement. If anything it widens the exposure, because a larger permitted response means more records leave the system on the request where authorisation was wrong.
distractors.E: Retained payloads establish what happened after it has happened. They prevent neither an unauthorised read nor an unintended reversal, and a quarterly cadence means the discovery is months behind the event.

questions.question: A hospital's discharge-summary assistant retrieves the patient's entire record — including unrelated historical episodes, next-of-kin contact details and billing notes — on the reasoning that additional context can only help the summary. What is the strongest objection at review?

options.A: Retrieval is the wrong mechanism here and the model should be fine-tuned on the record corpus instead
options.B: Only the minimum necessary data belongs in the context window; everything beyond what the summary requires enlarges the exposure without improving the output
options.C: The record should be condensed before it enters context so that it fits more comfortably
options.D: The assistant should be instructed to disregard the portions of the record that are not relevant to discharge

rationale.correct: Passing only the minimum necessary data into the context window is an integration rule precisely because the tempting default is the opposite. Billing notes and next-of-kin details cannot improve a discharge summary, so every one of those tokens is exposure bought for nothing — and the exposure is real, since context reaches logs, traces and any subprocessor in the path. Narrowing retrieval to what the summary requires reduces the blast radius of every downstream component at once.

distractors.A: Training on patient records would embed the exposure permanently rather than scope it per request, which makes the concern considerably harder to address, not easier.
distractors.C: Condensing reduces the token count while keeping the same categories of personal data in scope. The material still leaves the record system and still travels through everything downstream.
distractors.D: Asking the model to ignore data it has already been given does not un-send it. The data is in the request, the logs and the trace regardless of whether the model attends to it.

questions.question: An energy trading desk's assistant has been live for a fortnight. A trader formally disputes one of its recommendations. Engineers find they cannot establish which market data was retrieved or which tools were called for that session, because instrumentation had been scheduled for after the system stabilised. What does this episode demonstrate?

options.A: The dispute can be settled by re-running the same query today and comparing what comes back
options.B: Observability instrumentation belongs at design time rather than after the first incident, because the evidence needed to answer a dispute has to already exist when the dispute arrives
options.C: A longer retention period on the existing application logs would have covered this situation
options.D: The assistant should be withdrawn from the desk until instrumentation has been added

rationale.correct: Instrumentation is not a hardening step that follows stabilisation, it is the mechanism by which a system can be answered for at all. The evidence a dispute needs is generated at the moment of the session and cannot be reconstructed later, so scheduling it for afterwards guarantees the first dispute is the one that cannot be answered. Building it at design time is what makes the eventual incident investigable rather than merely regrettable.

distractors.A: Re-running the query today exercises today's market data and today's retrieval index. It produces a new answer rather than evidence about the disputed one, and on a trading desk the inputs have certainly moved.
distractors.C: Retention governs how long records survive. It cannot extend records that were never written, and what is missing here is the trace itself rather than its lifespan.
distractors.D: Withdrawal removes the capability without producing the missing evidence, and it treats a gap that can be closed forward as grounds for stopping.

questions.question: A cloud provider runs tens of thousands of assistant sessions each day. Engineers currently capture every full prompt, response and tool payload. Storage cost has become significant and failures are still difficult to locate in the volume. Which observability strategy fits this scale better?

options.A: Capture only the final response of each session and discard the intermediate steps
options.B: Structured traces with correlation identifiers and key metrics on every session, with full payload capture sampled and additionally triggered on error conditions
options.C: Disable capture in production and reproduce any reported failure in a staging environment
options.D: Treat customer-reported failures as the signal for which sessions are worth investigating

rationale.correct: At this volume the question is not whether to observe but what to keep at what fidelity. Structured traces with correlation identifiers on every session make failures findable and let one session be followed across services, while the expensive part — full payloads — is kept selectively, sampled for baseline visibility and triggered on errors so the sessions that matter are captured in full. Capturing everything and capturing nothing both make failures hard to find, for opposite reasons.

distractors.A: Agents fail in the middle. A final response with the tool calls and retrieved context stripped out records that something went wrong without any of the information needed to say why.
distractors.C: Staging does not hold the production inputs, the production index or the production tool state, which are usually what produced the failure. This discards the context that would have explained it.
distractors.D: Customer reports arrive after the damage, cover only failures a customer both noticed and bothered to report, and say nothing about the far larger population of quiet failures.

questions.question: A sports streaming service monitors its assistant through a single dashboard showing latency percentiles, error rate and token spend aggregated across all traffic. When a subscriber reports a poor answer, support cannot investigate it. When a regional spike appears, engineers cannot tell which sessions are behind it. What is missing from the design?

options.A: Additional panels on the aggregate dashboard, broken down by region and by feature
options.B: Per-request observability alongside the aggregate dashboards — the two answer different questions, and only the per-request layer can reconstruct an individual session
options.C: A longer retention window on the metrics so historical spikes remain queryable
options.D: A request that subscribers report the exact time of a poor answer so the aggregate charts can be read at that point

rationale.correct: Aggregate dashboards and per-request observability are separate layers answering separate questions, and at scale both are needed. Aggregates tell you the fleet's health and when something has changed; only a per-request trace can tell you what happened in the one session a subscriber is complaining about. The service has built the first layer thoroughly and has no instance of the second, which is why every question it currently cannot answer is about an individual session.

distractors.A: Finer breakdowns produce smaller aggregates. A regional panel narrows the population but still cannot reach the individual session, because no amount of grouping reconstructs one request's retrieved context and tool calls.
distractors.C: Longer retention preserves the same aggregate view for longer. It answers questions about trends over time, and every question raised here is about a specific session.
distractors.D: This asks subscribers to supply the precision the instrumentation should provide, and even a precise timestamp only locates a point on a chart that averages away the session in question.

questions.question: A government department is connecting Claude to a large number of internal systems including case management, payments, identity and correspondence. Different agencies own each system, tools will be added and retired frequently, and several AI applications across the department will need to reuse the same connections. Which integration approach fits these requirements?

options.A: Hard-code each system's REST interface into each application's tool definitions
options.B: Expose each system as an MCP server that any application in the department can connect to
options.C: Build a single middleware service that wraps every system behind one departmental endpoint
options.D: Grant Claude direct database access to each system so there are no interfaces to maintain

rationale.correct: This is the exact shape MCP is designed for: many systems, many consuming applications, ownership distributed across teams, and frequent tool churn. Each agency maintains its own server once and every application gets standardised, reusable access to it, so adding an application costs nothing per system and retiring a tool happens in one place. The alternative approaches all multiply work by either the number of applications or the number of systems.

distractors.A: Maintenance then scales with applications multiplied by systems, and every interface change has to be chased through each application separately, at which point they drift.
distractors.C: A single wrapper concentrates every agency's integration work into one team and one deployable, which becomes both the bottleneck for change and the component whose failure takes down everything.
distractors.D: Direct database access bypasses the business logic and access control the systems implement, so the department would be reimplementing both correctly in the assistant or living without them.

questions.question: A biotechnology firm needs three things: a conversational surface for scientists exploring published literature, an embedded classification call inside an existing laboratory pipeline, and a shared connector so any future internal tool can query the compound registry. A platform lead proposes standardising all three on one entry point for consistency. What should the architect advise?

options.A: Standardise on one entry point as proposed, since consistency reduces the long-run maintenance burden
options.B: Choose each entry point by the work it has to do — the three carry different core trade-offs — and name the trade-off out loud in each case so the firm knows later when to switch
options.C: Standardise all three on the direct API, since it offers the deepest control and everything else can be built on top of it
options.D: Defer the decision until the firm has run a pilot on each of the available entry points

rationale.correct: The entry points trade different things against each other — speed of setup against depth of control, a prebuilt interface against custom integration, breadth of tools against focus — and these three needs sit at different points on those trades. A conversational surface for scientists wants the prebuilt interface, an embedded call inside an owned pipeline wants the direct integration, and a connector meant for tools that do not exist yet wants discoverability. Naming the trade-off when the choice is made is what tells the firm later which choices are due to be revisited.

distractors.A: Consistency is a genuine benefit and here it is being applied as a rule in place of the analysis. One entry point across all three needs means at least two of them are served by something chosen for uniformity rather than fit.
distractors.C: Depth of control is the right criterion for the embedded pipeline call and the wrong one for the other two, where it means building a conversational interface and a discovery layer that already exist.
distractors.D: Piloting all of them costs the integration effort several times over to answer a question the trade-offs already answer, and it delays the two needs whose fit is not in doubt.

questions.question: A chemicals manufacturer's logistics agent must agree delivery windows with a haulier's independently operated scheduling agent. Neither company will expose its internal systems or tools to the other. Which connection approach fits this requirement best?

options.A: Register the haulier's scheduling tools directly in the manufacturer's tool catalogue
options.B: Agent-to-agent communication across an agreed protocol boundary, with each agent mediating access to its own organisation's systems
options.C: Exchange scheduling files each night and have each agent read whatever its counterpart last published
options.D: Replace both agents with a single shared agent operated by a neutral third party

rationale.correct: Coordination across an organisational trust boundary, where neither side will open its systems to the other, is what agent-to-agent communication exists for. Each agent becomes the boundary: it holds the access to its own organisation's systems and exposes only the negotiating behaviour, so the two can converge on a delivery window without either party gaining visibility of the other's internals.

distractors.A: Registering the haulier's tools locally is precisely the exposure the haulier has refused, and it would require the manufacturer to hold credentials into another company's scheduling system.
distractors.C: A nightly file exchange turns a negotiation into two monologues a day apart. Delivery windows move within the day, so each side would be committing against a picture that is already stale.
distractors.D: A shared third-party agent requires both companies to grant that operator the access neither will grant each other, and it introduces a commercial dependency neither has asked for.

questions.question: For each integration need, identify the most suitable connection mechanism. Options may be used more than once.

scenarios.text: Several AI applications across a group need standardised, reusable access to the shared asset register.
A nightly batch job pushes reconciled ledger entries into the data warehouse, with no model involvement in the transfer itself.
Two autonomous agents owned by different companies must agree berth allocation without exposing their internal systems to each other.
A newly published internal policy library should be discoverable and usable by any current or future agent in the organisation.
An existing microservice needs to call the model once to classify an inbound document inside its own tightly controlled pipeline.

rationale.correct: The deciding question in each case is who needs to find the capability and where the trust boundary sits. The asset register and the policy library both need standardised, discoverable access for consumers that are not all known yet, which is what an MCP server provides and what makes the fourth case an MCP question even though nothing consumes it today. The ledger transfer and the single classification call are deterministic, tightly scoped operations inside a pipeline the organisation owns, so a direct API integration is correct and a discovery layer would be machinery with nothing to discover. Berth allocation crosses an organisational boundary between two autonomous agents that will not open their systems to each other, which is the defining agent-to-agent case.

questions.question: An HR services provider is weighing progressive discovery, where tools and reference material load on demand, against loading everything up front. Which TWO situations most strongly favour progressive discovery? (Select TWO)

options.A: The catalogue of tools and reference material is large, and only a small subset of it is relevant to any single request
options.B: The context budget is constrained and loading everything up front is already degrading response quality
options.C: The service uses three tools, all of which are needed on every request
options.D: Requests must complete in a single model invocation with no intermediate steps
options.E: Per-request latency must be minimised above every other consideration

rationale.correct: Progressive discovery earns its extra round trips under two conditions, and they usually appear together. When only a small slice of a large catalogue is relevant to any one request, loading the whole catalogue spends most of the context on material that request will never use. And when the context budget is tight enough that up-front loading is already costing response quality, the trade has become favourable: a little more latency in exchange for a prompt the model can actually attend to.

distractors.C: With three tools all needed every time, there is nothing to discover and nothing to defer. Discovery machinery here adds round trips to reach a conclusion that was never in doubt.
distractors.D: Discovery is intermediate steps by definition. A hard single-invocation constraint rules the approach out rather than favouring it.
distractors.E: Progressive discovery trades latency for context quality, so making latency the overriding consideration argues against it. That is a real reason to choose otherwise, not a reason to choose this.

questions.question: A semiconductor fab's assistant has three tools whose purposes substantially overlap: one returns lot status, one queries lots by attribute, and one looks a lot up by identifier. The agent frequently invokes the wrong one of the three. Which change most directly reduces the error?

options.A: Instruct the agent to prefer whichever of the three appears first in the list when it is uncertain
options.B: Consolidate the overlapping tools and rewrite what remains so each tool's purpose, inputs and boundaries are explicit and non-overlapping
options.C: Add a further tool whose job is to select which of the three the agent should call
options.D: Replace all three with one generic execution tool that accepts a free-text command

rationale.correct: Selection errors between related tools come from overlap and ambiguity, so the fix works on both: remove the overlap by consolidating what does the same job, and remove the ambiguity by making each surviving tool's purpose, inputs and boundaries explicit. When three tools can each plausibly answer the same question, no amount of care at selection time makes the choice determinate, because the ambiguity is in the catalogue rather than in the reasoning.

distractors.A: A tie-break rule makes the wrong choice consistent rather than less frequent, and it hides the ambiguity behind an ordering nobody will remember is load-bearing.
distractors.C: A selector tool leaves three ambiguous tools in place and adds a fourth component that has to resolve the same ambiguity, now with less context about the request than the agent had.
distractors.D: Collapsing typed tools into a free-text command surface discards the schemas that make invalid calls detectable, so selection errors become execution errors that fail later and less clearly.

questions.question: A commercial property firm's lease-analysis assistant splits each lease into fixed-size blocks for retrieval. Retrieval frequently returns clause fragments whose meaning depends on defined terms and cross-references located elsewhere in the same lease, and answer quality suffers as a result. Which change most directly addresses this?

options.A: Reduce the block size so that retrieval becomes more precise
options.B: Adopt structure-aware chunking aligned to clauses and schedules, with metadata linking defined terms and cross-references
options.C: Retrieve a much larger number of blocks per question so the missing context is probably somewhere among them
options.D: Replace retrieval with a keyword index built over clause headings only

rationale.correct: The failure is structural rather than statistical: a lease clause means what it means because of definitions and cross-references elsewhere in the document, and fixed-size blocks cut those links arbitrarily. Chunking along the document's own boundaries keeps each retrieved unit interpretable, and linkage metadata carries the definitions and referenced clauses along with it, so the assistant reads a clause with the context a lawyer would read it with.

distractors.A: Smaller blocks sever more relationships, not fewer. Precision improves on the fragment while the interpretive context it depends on becomes even more likely to sit outside it.
distractors.C: Flooding the context raises the chance that a definition happens to be included, without any guarantee that the one this clause depends on is among them, and it pays a large token cost for a probabilistic improvement.
distractors.D: Headings describe what a clause is called rather than what it says, so this discards the semantic retrieval that is working for the majority of questions in order to address a subset.

questions.question: A fashion retailer's merchandising assistant uses purely semantic retrieval over the product catalogue. Buyers searching by exact style code frequently receive visually similar but incorrect products, while natural-language searches such as requests for lightweight summer outerwear work well. Which retrieval strategy resolves this?

options.A: Replace semantic retrieval with keyword search across the whole catalogue
options.B: Hybrid retrieval combining exact and keyword matching with semantic search, weighted according to the shape of the query
options.C: Adopt a larger embedding model so that style codes embed more distinctly from one another
options.D: Ask buyers to describe the garment in words rather than searching by style code

rationale.correct: The two query types have opposite requirements. A style code is an identifier where only an exact match is correct and near-misses are precisely the wrong answer, while a description of a garment is exactly where semantic similarity earns its place. Hybrid retrieval routes each query to the matching that suits its shape rather than forcing both through one mechanism, which is why it fixes the codes without disturbing the searches that already work.

distractors.A: This trades one failure for the other. Keyword search handles the codes and then cannot serve a buyer describing a garment rather than naming it, which is the majority of current successful use.
distractors.C: Better embeddings make similar codes slightly less confusable and leave the underlying mismatch intact, because the requirement for an identifier is exactness rather than proximity.
distractors.D: This asks buyers to stop using the most precise input they have, and pushes the cost of the system's limitation onto the people it was built to serve.

questions.question: After a nightly catalogue refresh, a museum archive assistant intermittently answers from records that have since been superseded. Which TWO measures most directly address this? (Select TWO)

options.A: An automated re-indexing pipeline that validates completeness and embedding consistency after every refresh
options.B: Version metadata carried in the index, with retrieval filtering out superseded records
options.C: Running the refresh a second time each night in case the first pass was incomplete
options.D: A weekly manual spot-check of a handful of the assistant's answers
options.E: Lowering the temperature so that the assistant relies less on the retrieved records

rationale.correct: Intermittent staleness after a refresh has two possible sources and these address one each. A validated re-indexing pipeline stops incomplete or inconsistent embeddings entering the index in the first place, which is the write-side failure. Version metadata with retrieval filtering stops superseded records being served even when they do linger, which is the read-side failure. Either alone leaves the other path open, which is why the symptom is intermittent.

distractors.C: Repeating an unvalidated process gives two chances to fail silently rather than one, and without a completeness check neither pass can report whether it succeeded.
distractors.D: A weekly sample of a handful of answers is far too sparse to catch a defect that appears intermittently after a nightly job, and it detects rather than prevents.
distractors.E: Sampling temperature does not influence which records retrieval returns. Relying less on retrieved content would in any case make answers less grounded rather than more current.

questions.question: An airline is putting a disruption-management assistant into service before the winter season, when the upstream systems it depends on are historically least reliable. Which TWO measures belong in the initial design rather than being added after the first outage? (Select TWO)

options.A: Retries with backoff on transient upstream failures, and a fallback chain so a degraded answer is still produced when the primary path is unavailable
options.B: Circuit breakers that stop calling a dependency that is already failing rather than queueing behind it
options.C: A status page telling crews when the assistant is unavailable
options.D: A post-incident review process to be followed after each outage
options.E: A longer request timeout so that slow dependencies have more time to respond

rationale.correct: Resiliency primitives belong in the initial design because retrofitting them means changing the call path of a system already in service, usually during the incident that proved they were needed. Retries with backoff and a fallback chain keep the assistant useful through transient failures and partial outages, and circuit breakers stop a failing dependency from consuming the assistant's capacity and turning one system's outage into everything's. The season the airline has chosen is exactly when both will be exercised.

distractors.C: A status page tells crews the assistant is unavailable. It is honest and it is not resiliency, because the capability is still gone at the moment disruption management most needs it.
distractors.D: Post-incident review improves the next design cycle. It operates entirely after the outage and changes nothing about how the system behaves during one.
distractors.E: A longer timeout converts a fast failure into a slow one and holds resources open while the dependency struggles, which tends to spread the failure rather than absorb it.

questions.question: Adding a re-ranking stage to a freight-quoting assistant's retrieval pipeline raises answer accuracy from 84% to 93% but adds 500 ms to each request. The contractual SLA is 3 seconds and current p95 latency is 1.4 seconds. How should the architect reason about this trade-off?

options.A: Reject re-ranking, because added latency should never be accepted in a customer-facing system
options.B: Adopt re-ranking: quantified against the SLA, the accuracy gain is material and 500 ms still leaves clear headroom below 3 seconds, so adopt it and monitor p95
options.C: Adopt re-ranking only for the subset of quotes to which the SLA does not apply
options.D: Defer the decision until the SLA can be renegotiated to allow more time

rationale.correct: The method is to quantify both sides against the budget that actually constrains the system. The accuracy gain is large enough to change how often a quote is right, the latency cost is known, and adding it to the current p95 still lands well inside the contractual SLA with room for the variance that real traffic brings. That is a decision the data supports, and the follow-up is to monitor p95 so the headroom is watched rather than assumed.

distractors.A: This is a rule standing in for the analysis. Latency is a budget rather than a value to be minimised without limit, and refusing to spend any of it forfeits improvements the budget can comfortably absorb.
distractors.C: Splitting behaviour by whether the SLA applies means two quality levels for the same product, and the quotes that fall outside the SLA are unlikely to be the ones where accuracy matters least.
distractors.D: Renegotiating a contract to buy headroom the system already has inverts the problem. The measurement shows the change fits within the existing commitment.

questions.question: A medical device company is building an assistant that drafts sections of regulatory submissions. The plan is to build the pipeline, get it working end to end, and then write an evaluation suite once behaviour has settled. What should the architect change about that plan?

options.A: Nothing, since an eval suite written against unsettled behaviour would only have to be rewritten later
options.B: Write the eval suite first, so that it defines acceptance rather than describing whatever the finished pipeline happens to do
options.C: Write the eval suite alongside the pipeline, seeding it with the pipeline's own early outputs as the initial cases
