options.D: Replace the eval suite with a review by a regulatory affairs specialist before each submission goes out

rationale.correct: An eval suite written first is a statement of what the system must do; one written afterwards tends to become a description of what it already does, because the easiest cases to write down are the ones in front of you. Writing it first makes acceptance a decision taken while it can still be argued about on its merits, and it means the pipeline is built against a target rather than measured against its own habits.

distractors.A: Behaviour settling is the outcome the suite is supposed to drive, not a precondition for writing it. Waiting means the first version of the suite is shaped by whatever the pipeline converged on unsupervised.
distractors.C: Seeding the suite from the pipeline's own outputs makes the system its own standard. Anything it does consistently becomes the expected result, including its consistent mistakes.
distractors.D: Specialist review catches problems in the submission in front of the reviewer. It gives no coverage against regression when a prompt changes, and it cannot be re-run against a proposed change before that change ships.

questions.question: A lender is assembling the golden dataset for a credit decisioning assistant. Which TWO compositions give the most trustworthy signal? (Select TWO)

options.A: Anonymised real applications sampled from live intake, so the distribution matches what the assistant will actually meet
options.B: Deliberately constructed edge cases and high-risk scenarios, labelled by credit specialists
options.C: Cases generated by the model itself from the lending policy document
options.D: The worked examples already embedded in the system prompt, since the assistant must at minimum handle those
options.E: A set frozen at launch, so that results stay comparable as the assistant changes

rationale.correct: These two cover the two things an evaluation has to say something about. Real sampled applications establish how the assistant performs on the distribution it will actually meet, which synthetic cases systematically misrepresent. Constructed edge cases labelled by specialists establish how it behaves at the boundaries, which real sampling reaches too rarely to measure. Common-path competence and failure-surface behaviour are different questions and each needs its own material.

distractors.C: Cases generated from the policy document inherit that document's blind spots exactly, so the assistant is tested against the same assumptions it was built from and the gaps stay invisible.
distractors.D: Testing on the examples already in the prompt measures whether the assistant can reproduce material it has been given. Passing proves memorisation rather than capability.
distractors.E: Comparability is a genuine benefit, and a frozen set drifts away from live intake as products and applicant behaviour change, so it slowly becomes a measure of the past. The golden dataset has to be kept current with the system it gates.

questions.question: For each evaluation need, identify the most appropriate primary method. Options may be used more than once.

scenarios.text: Confirming that a revised system prompt has not regressed extraction accuracy on the cases the team has already decided matter, before anything reaches users.
Scoring tone and helpfulness across many thousands of weekly support replies against a written style rubric.
Establishing whether a new summarisation approach improves user task completion, where offline results for the two approaches are tied and the primary metric has been fixed in advance.
Confirming that an assistant holding database tools cannot be induced by hostile user input into returning another tenant's records.
Verifying that a model version upgrade has not degraded performance on the organisation's highest-risk document types.

rationale.correct: The first and last are the same question asked about different changes: a regression check against a labelled set the organisation has already decided matters, which is exactly what a golden dataset is for, and both are gates that must clear before exposure rather than after. Tone across many thousands of replies is subjective quality at a volume no human panel covers, so a rubric-driven judge scores everything and periodic human ratings keep that judge honest. The summarisation comparison is the case where offline measurement is exhausted and only real user behaviour can settle it, which is what a controlled production comparison exists for, and it is a valid experiment only because the metric was fixed beforehand. The tenant-isolation question is a boundary property, and boundary properties are established by trying to breach them rather than by measuring average-case accuracy.

questions.question: A marketplace's steering group asks whether its new seller-onboarding assistant is good enough to launch. The team has warm feedback from pilot sellers and no formal measures of any kind. What should the architect establish first?

options.A: A published benchmark score for the underlying model, so the group has an objective figure to consider
options.B: Task-specific evaluation metrics tied to business outcomes — onboarding completion rate, document rejection rate, time to first listing — each with an agreed launch threshold
options.C: A launch date, on the basis that the criteria will become obvious once real sellers are using it
options.D: A comparison of the assistant's inference cost against the cost of the current manual onboarding process

rationale.correct: Good enough is not a property a system has, it is a comparison against a threshold somebody agreed in advance. Metrics tied to the outcomes the marketplace actually cares about make the launch decision answerable, and agreeing the thresholds before the numbers are known is what stops the bar moving to wherever the results landed. Without that, the steering group is being asked to approve on impression.

distractors.A: A benchmark measures the model in general rather than this assistant on this task. A strong score would tell the group nothing about onboarding completion, and a weak one nothing either.
distractors.C: The criteria do not become obvious in production, they become contested there. Launching first means the definition of success gets written after the results are visible, by whoever is most invested in the answer.
distractors.D: Cost against the manual process is a real and separate question. It establishes whether the assistant is worth running, not whether it is good enough to be trusted with sellers.

questions.question: A broadcaster must evaluate tone and editorial-guideline alignment across many thousands of automatically generated programme descriptions each week. Reviewing all of them by hand is not feasible. Which evaluation methodology fits?

options.A: Exact matching of each description against a library of approved phrasings
options.B: An LLM-as-judge rubric scored against the editorial guidelines, calibrated periodically against a sample of ratings from human editors
options.C: Full human review of every description, absorbing the throughput cost as the price of quality
options.D: Omit tone evaluation, since tone is subjective and therefore cannot be measured

rationale.correct: Subjective quality at volume needs a mixed methodology: a rubric-driven judge scores every output, which is the only way to get coverage at this scale, and periodic human ratings on a sample keep the judge anchored to what editors actually mean by on-tone. The calibration is what makes the approach trustworthy rather than merely scalable, because an uncalibrated judge drifts and nobody notices.

distractors.A: Matching against approved phrasings can only recognise descriptions that reuse existing wording. Every genuinely new description scores as a failure, which makes the measure useless precisely where the assistant is doing its job.
distractors.C: This absorbs a cost the broadcaster has already established it cannot absorb. Declaring the throughput problem acceptable does not make the reviews happen.
distractors.D: Tone is subjective and it is also measurable, which is what a rubric is for. Treating subjectivity as a reason not to measure abandons a requirement the editorial guidelines already state.

questions.question: A travel booking platform's revised prompt outperforms the current one on the offline suite. The team wants production evidence before replacing it everywhere, and proposes shipping it to half of traffic, watching the dashboards for a week and then deciding. What is missing from that proposal?

options.A: Nothing of substance — a week at half of traffic is ample exposure to see the effect
options.B: The primary metric and the sample size have to be identified before the experiment runs, or the decision is made by whichever dashboard happens to look most convincing afterwards
options.C: The experiment should run across all traffic instead, so that significance is reached sooner
options.D: The offline suite should be re-run several more times first, to raise confidence in the original result

rationale.correct: Exposure is not the constraint here, interpretation is. Identifying the primary metric and the sample size before the experiment runs is what turns a week of traffic into evidence, because it fixes in advance what would count as a win and how much data is needed to believe it. Deciding afterwards, with several dashboards available, means the result is chosen rather than measured.

distractors.A: Ample exposure produces ample data and no decision rule. With enough metrics on screen, a week of traffic will support whichever conclusion is looked for.
distractors.C: Running across all traffic removes the control group, so there is nothing to compare against and the platform has taken on full exposure to a change it cannot yet evaluate.
distractors.D: Repeating the offline suite re-measures the same distribution and raises confidence in a result that was never the thing in doubt. The open question is whether the offline gain transfers to production.

questions.question: A port operator plans to move its berth-scheduling assistant onto a newly released model version. Offline spot checks against a handful of representative cases look fine. Which rollout practice best protects production quality?

options.A: Switch all traffic at once, since the newer version is the more capable one overall
options.B: Run the full evaluation suite against the new version, then roll out gradually behind a canary with regression monitoring before full cutover
options.C: Adopt the new version for newly onboarded shipping lines only, leaving established lines on the current version indefinitely
options.D: Wait two quarters until other operators have reported their experience of the new version

rationale.correct: A model version change is a regression risk, and spot checks against a handful of cases are far too coarse to detect one. The full suite catches task-level regressions the spot checks miss, and a canary with regression monitoring bounds the exposure to whatever the suite did not cover. The two together are what make the change reversible before it reaches the whole berth schedule.

distractors.A: More capable in general does not mean better on this operator's scheduling task, and a full switch removes any opportunity to discover the difference before it affects every berth.
distractors.C: Splitting by shipping line leaves two versions running permanently with no plan to converge, which doubles the surface to maintain while protecting neither group.
distractors.D: Waiting for other operators forfeits the improvements for two quarters and gathers evidence about their workloads rather than this one, which is not the evidence needed.

questions.question: Leadership asks an agricultural technology company to reduce assistant inference cost by a third. The team's first proposal is to move every workload onto the smallest model. What should the architect do before accepting that proposal?

options.A: Accept it, since the model tier is the only cost lever that moves the total meaningfully
options.B: Analyse token usage and cost per workload from production traces to identify the dominant cost driver, then apply the lever that targets it, evaluating quality impact at each step
options.C: Reject the reduction target, on the grounds that any material cost cut will degrade quality
options.D: Cut the maximum output tokens across every workload by a third

rationale.correct: Optimise from evidence rather than intuition. Trace-level analysis shows whether the spend is actually in context size, cache misses, output length or model tier, and those call for different levers with very different quality consequences. Frequently the dominant cost driver turns out to be a large repeated prefix that caching removes at no quality cost at all, which is a better outcome than the tier change and would never have been found by assuming.

distractors.A: Model tier is one lever among several and is often not the dominant one. Assuming it is means paying for the cut in capability when a cheaper source of savings may have been available untouched.
distractors.C: This refuses a legitimate business mandate on an assumption that has not been tested. Some cost reductions carry no quality cost, and the analysis is what distinguishes those from the ones that do.
distractors.D: Truncating output uniformly cuts spend and cuts every response that legitimately needed the length, which converts a cost problem into a quality problem distributed unpredictably across workloads.

questions.question: An aged-care provider's care-note summarisation pilot has run smoothly in a single home. The board now wants to commit publicly to a rollout date across every home in the group. What must be established before that commitment is made?

options.A: Confirmation that staff at the pilot home are satisfied with the summaries they have been receiving
options.B: Cost and latency modelled at full production volume, so the commitment is made against the operating envelope the system will actually run in
options.C: A phased onboarding schedule so that homes come online gradually and problems surface early
options.D: Approval to increase engineering headcount so that the rollout can be supported

rationale.correct: A pilot in one home answers whether the summaries are useful. It does not answer whether the design survives the volume of every home, and per-request cost and latency that are unremarkable at pilot scale are exactly the figures that become binding constraints at group scale. Modelling the envelope before the date is announced is far cheaper than discovering it after the board has committed publicly.

distractors.A: Pilot satisfaction is evidence the summaries are good and no evidence at all about what happens to cost or response time when the request volume rises by the number of homes in the group.
distractors.C: A phased schedule is sensible delivery practice and it manages the consequences of a commitment rather than establishing whether the commitment is sound. Phasing a rollout that cannot afford its own volume only slows the arrival of the problem.
distractors.D: Headcount addresses how much work the rollout can absorb. It says nothing about the per-request economics or the response time the system will deliver at scale.

questions.question: A dental group wants early warning of quality degradation in its retrieval-based clinical guidance assistant, ideally before clinicians notice anything. Which signal is the most useful leading indicator?

options.A: A rise in formal complaints submitted through the practice feedback form
options.B: A decline in retrieval relevance scores and a rise in the rate of no-grounded-answer outcomes in the pipeline's own telemetry
options.C: A monthly review by a clinical lead of a sample of the assistant's answers
options.D: An alert when inference spend departs from its established norm

rationale.correct: Retrieval relevance and grounding rates are internal to the pipeline, which is what makes them leading: they move when the retrieval layer starts returning weaker material, and that happens before the weaker material has been turned into answers clinicians act on. Everything a clinician could notice is by definition downstream of the answer already being produced, so any signal collected there is reporting damage rather than predicting it.

distractors.A: A complaint means a clinician already received a poor answer and was sufficiently troubled to report it. That is the outcome the group is trying to get ahead of, and most poor answers never generate one.
distractors.C: Monthly sampling is a detective control on a slow cycle. It will eventually find a degradation that started weeks earlier, by which time the intervening answers have all been delivered.
distractors.D: Spend tracks usage and pricing rather than correctness. A retrieval layer returning increasingly irrelevant material can degrade quality substantially while costing very nearly the same.

questions.question: A managed security provider is designing the pre-production evaluation framework for an assistant that will operate in a regulated domain. Which TWO components matter most? (Select TWO)

options.A: A golden dataset labelled by domain experts, covering both typical and high-risk scenarios
options.B: An adversarial test suite probing safety boundaries, injected instructions and policy-violating requests
options.C: A live demonstration to the executive committee using selected strong examples
options.D: A benchmark comparing the model's general knowledge against competitor models
options.E: A user-satisfaction survey administered once the assistant has launched

rationale.correct: A regulated deployment has to establish two different properties before exposure. Expert-labelled golden data shows competence on the cases that occur, including the high-risk ones that occur rarely enough to be missed by sampling alone. An adversarial suite shows that the boundaries hold when somebody is actively trying to break them, which average-case accuracy never reveals because the average case is not hostile. Neither substitutes for the other.

distractors.C: A demonstration on selected examples establishes that good outputs are achievable. That was never in question, and the selection guarantees the framework's weak points are the material not shown.
distractors.D: General knowledge benchmarks measure the model against other models rather than this assistant against this domain's requirements, so a good result carries no assurance about the regulated task.
distractors.E: A satisfaction survey collects opinion after the assistant has been in front of users, which is after the regulated risk has already been taken.

questions.question: A textile manufacturer's assistant is asked to confirm a supplier's compliance certificate. The lookup tool returns no matching record. The assistant replies with a certificate number and an expiry date. Which failure class is this, and what follows from that classification?

options.A: A prompt failure — the instructions were not specific enough about the required output format
options.B: A hallucination — content was fabricated rather than grounded in the tool result, so the remedy is grounding discipline together with an explicit path for the empty-result case
options.C: A model mismatch — certificate verification exceeds what this model tier handles reliably
options.D: A retrieval failure — the certificate does exist and the lookup did not locate it

rationale.correct: Classifying the failure is what selects the remedy, and confidently producing data that no source supplied is a hallucination whatever else is also true. The tool returned nothing and the assistant produced a number and a date, which means the output was generated rather than grounded. The remedy follows directly: require answers to be grounded in tool results, and give the empty result an explicit handling path so that not found is an outcome the assistant can express rather than a gap it fills.

distractors.A: Output format is genuinely underspecified, and tightening it produces a well-formatted fabrication. The defect is that content was invented, not that it was presented badly.
distractors.C: Nothing here suggests the task is beyond the tier. Reporting that a lookup returned nothing is not a demanding capability, and a more capable model given no result can fabricate just as readily.
distractors.D: This asserts a fact not in evidence. The scenario states the lookup returned no matching record, and treating that as a false negative reinterprets the one thing that is known in order to protect the assistant.

questions.question: A brewery group's demand-forecasting assistant has degraded intermittently over two weeks. The model version, the prompts and the application code are all unchanged over that period. Which TWO data sources are most useful for diagnosing the cause? (Select TWO)

options.A: End-to-end traces of the affected sessions, including retrieved context and tool inputs and outputs
options.B: Analysis of the input distribution for drift — question types, formats or languages the assistant was not designed for
options.C: The number of requests served per day across the period
options.D: A survey of the demand planners who noticed the degradation
options.E: Uptime statistics for the model endpoint

rationale.correct: With the code, the model and the prompts all unchanged, the cause is almost certainly in what is flowing through the system rather than in the system itself. Traces show what actually happened inside the failing sessions — what was retrieved, what the tools returned — which is the only place the change will be visible. Drift analysis answers the complementary question of whether the inputs themselves have moved, which is the usual reason a stable system starts behaving differently.

distractors.C: Request volume describes how much the assistant was used. A quality change can happen at any volume, and volume alone cannot distinguish a degraded answer from a good one.
distractors.D: Planners can say when the answers felt wrong and roughly about what. They cannot say what was retrieved or what the tools returned, which is the information the diagnosis actually turns on.
distractors.E: Uptime measures availability. The assistant was available throughout — it was answering, and answering worse, which uptime cannot express.

questions.question: A utility's billing assistant is reviewed after it disclosed a customer's payment-arrangement details to a caller who was not the account holder. The team is surprised, pointing out that the model is trained not to reveal personal information. What does the incident actually reveal about the design?

options.A: The model tier is the constraint, and a more capable model would have recognised the caller was not the account holder
options.B: Safety is a stack of layers rather than a setting: training covers broad harm and never saw this utility's identity-verification rules, so that rule was enforced in no layer at all — which is the silent failure the layered model exists to prevent
options.C: The system prompt should state the identity-verification rule more emphatically than it currently does
options.D: The incident should be recorded and brought to the next governance meeting for a decision on remediation

rationale.correct: Training reduces broad harm across every request and it has never seen this utility's domain policy, its data rules or its authorisation model. Assuming a rule is enforced when it lives in no layer is the dangerous failure precisely because it is silent: the system behaves correctly for as long as nothing tests the assumption, and the first test is an incident. The design needs the rule to exist somewhere it is actually applied, which means identity verification enforced before the account data ever enters the conversation.

distractors.A: A more capable model would make this disclosure less often and would still have no way to verify who is on the telephone, because that determination lives in systems the model cannot see.
distractors.C: Emphasis in the prompt asks an instruction to perform an authorisation check. It may hold most of the time, and most of the time is not what a verification control is for.
distractors.D: Recording the incident is appropriate and it operates entirely after the disclosure. It adds a review cadence rather than a layer, so the next caller is protected by the same nothing.

questions.question: A logistics operator's warehouse agent can read stock records and can also call tools that adjust inventory counts and cancel outbound shipments. Its only guardrail is output screening, which checks replies against policy before they are displayed. During an assurance exercise, a supplier-submitted document in the retrieval corpus caused the agent to cancel a live shipment. Output screening recorded no violation. What does this reveal about the design?

options.A: The output screening policy was too permissive and should be extended to cover shipment cancellations
options.B: The guarded path has only one of its three control points: input screening and tool-call authorization answer different questions from output screening, and the harm travelled the tool-call path, which was ungoverned
options.C: Screening was applied at the wrong stage and should be relocated to the retrieval step instead
options.D: The retrieval corpus should be restricted to documents authored inside the operator's own organisation

rationale.correct: A guarded path has three control points — input screening, output screening and tool-call authorization — and they answer different questions, so one filter at the end does not cover the other two. The damaging event here was a tool invocation executing against a real system: by the time any text reached output screening the shipment was already cancelled, and a truthful reply about it would not read as a violation. The remedy is authorization on the tool call itself, set to fail closed for irreversible operations, with retrieved supplier content treated as untrusted data that holds no instruction authority.

distractors.A: Broadening the policy does not change which channel it inspects. A more thorough output filter would still have found nothing objectionable in the reply, because the reply was accurate.
distractors.C: Screening retrieved documents is a genuine third control and worth adding. Relocating the single control rather than adding to it leaves the tool-call path exactly as ungoverned as it is now, with the output path newly uncovered.
distractors.D: Restricting the corpus to internal documents narrows one source of untrusted content without changing the trust model, and it discards the supplier material the agent needs. Internally authored documents can carry injected text too.

questions.question: A facilities management firm's maintenance assistant answers from a corpus that includes method statements supplied by contractors. A security review finds that one method statement contains text directing the assistant to disclose its configuration, and the assistant partially complied. Which design principle does this violate?

options.A: A retrieval corpus must contain only documents authored inside the organisation
options.B: Retrieved content is untrusted input: it must be structurally delimited as data and never granted instruction-level authority
options.C: System prompts must be held encrypted so their contents cannot be disclosed
options.D: Retrieval must be suspended for any document that contains imperative sentences

rationale.correct: The violated principle is trust separation. Anything retrieved is input from outside the trust boundary, so it must be delimited as data the assistant reads about rather than instructions the assistant follows. Once that distinction is structural, a method statement containing directive text is simply a document that contains directive text, which is exactly what it is. The same principle underlies injection defence everywhere: the question is never whether hostile content can appear, it is whether appearing grants it authority.

distractors.A: Contractor method statements are the material the assistant exists to answer from, so excluding external documents removes the capability. It also assumes internal authorship implies safety, which does not hold.
distractors.C: Protecting the prompt at rest addresses confidentiality of the stored artefact. The assistant disclosed its configuration through the conversation, a path encryption never touches, and the same injection could have directed a tool call instead.
distractors.D: Method statements are written as instructions to people, so this rule would exclude nearly the whole corpus while still admitting any injection phrased as description.

questions.question: A clinical research organisation is hardening a trial-data assistant whose tools can read study records, amend them, and unblind treatment allocation. Which TWO measures most directly limit what a successful prompt injection could achieve? (Select TWO)

options.A: Scope the tool surface to least privilege, so that amendment and unblinding are not available to the assistant's own credentials at all
options.B: Place every irreversible operation behind an explicit approval gate that fails closed when the approval is absent
options.C: Move to a more capable model, since more capable models are not susceptible to injection
options.D: Log every retrieved document so that injections can be identified in review afterwards
options.E: Set the temperature to zero so the assistant does not act on adversarial content

rationale.correct: These two accept that an injection may succeed and bound what it can reach, which is the only reliable posture. Least-privilege scoping means the destructive capabilities are not held by the component under attack, so no instruction can invoke what the credentials cannot perform. An approval gate that fails closed means an irreversible operation stops in the absence of a decision rather than proceeding, so the failure direction is chosen deliberately rather than inherited. Unblinding a trial is exactly the operation that must not proceed by default.

distractors.C: Capability does not confer immunity to injection. This substitutes an assumption for a control and leaves the destructive tools attached to the assistant either way.
distractors.D: Logging retrieved documents is worth doing and it identifies the injection after the amendment or unblinding has already occurred. It is detective where the requirement is preventative.
distractors.E: Sampling temperature governs variation in wording, not whether the assistant treats retrieved text as an instruction. A deterministic assistant follows an injected instruction just as reliably.

questions.question: An online lender deploys an assistant that drafts responses to borrower complaints. The regulator's requirement is that no incorrect financial commitment reaches a borrower. Which TWO controls most directly address that requirement? (Select TWO)

options.A: An output guardrail that blocks any commitment expressed outside approved policy language from being produced at all
options.B: Mandatory human review and approval before any drafted response is sent to a borrower
options.C: Logging every draft to a warehouse for review each quarter
options.D: Training complaint handlers to write better prompts for the assistant
options.E: A standing disclaimer on each response noting that any figures given are indicative

rationale.correct: The requirement is absolute — nothing incorrect may reach a borrower — so the controls are layered on the same risk rather than chosen between. A preventative guardrail constrains what can be drafted, removing whole classes of wrong commitment before they exist. Mandatory human approval catches the cases the guardrail's rules do not anticipate, which is every regulator's real concern. Prevention narrows what reaches the reviewer, and the reviewer covers what prevention could not foresee.

distractors.C: Quarterly review discovers an incorrect commitment months after the borrower received and possibly relied on it, which is precisely the outcome the requirement forbids.
distractors.D: Better prompting improves the average quality of drafts. It offers no guarantee about any individual draft, and the requirement is stated as a guarantee.
distractors.E: A disclaimer attached to an incorrect commitment does not prevent the borrower receiving it, and a regulator is unlikely to accept boilerplate as the reason a wrong figure was sent.

questions.question: For each risk scenario, identify the most appropriate primary control. Options may be used more than once.

scenarios.text: An assistant must never emit a customer's full bank account number in any response, under any circumstances.
An agent recommends whether to approve a commercial loan, and each recommendation carries significant financial and regulatory consequence.
Compliance must be able to demonstrate, a year later, exactly what an agent did and why during a disputed transaction.
A content generator must be prevented from producing marketing claims that breach advertising standards before anything is displayed.
Leadership wants early detection if the assistant's refusal rate begins trending upward across the estate.

rationale.correct: Review is routed by stakes rather than by volume, and the three controls answer different questions. The first and fourth are absolutes stated as never and before display, which means they must be prevented rather than caught, because a control that detects them has already allowed the thing it forbids. The loan recommendation is a consequential judgement made one decision at a time, with low reversibility and a high cost of error, which is the profile that earns a person's attention — and sending only this class to a human is what keeps the queue readable. The third and fifth are about reconstruction after the fact and trend detection across the estate, neither of which prevents anything and both of which depend on records and metrics being collected while the events occur.

questions.question: A municipal authority's procurement assistant can draft supplier correspondence, update internal records, and raise purchase orders below a delegated value threshold. The authority wants human oversight without slowing every interaction. Where should the approval gate sit?

options.A: Before every action the assistant takes, so that nothing at all happens without approval
options.B: Before irreversible or high-impact external actions such as raising a purchase order, while low-risk drafting and internal record updates proceed automatically
options.C: After the purchase order has been raised, so that a reviewer can check it retrospectively
options.D: Before any action the assistant itself flags as uncertain, with the assistant deciding which those are

rationale.correct: The gate is placed by stakes, and reversibility is the sharpest of the three factors here. A draft can be edited and an internal record can be corrected, so neither needs a person standing in front of it. A purchase order is a commitment leaving the authority, which is where the cost of being wrong stops being recoverable. Gating exactly that class preserves the throughput that justifies the assistant while putting a person where the consequences are permanent.

distractors.A: Approving everything destroys the efficiency the assistant exists to create, and in practice it produces a queue of trivial approvals in which the significant ones are waved through unread.
distractors.C: Retrospective review happens after the commitment has left the authority. The reviewer can begin a correction process rather than prevent the error.
distractors.D: Delegating the gate decision to the assistant means the control depends on the component it is meant to check, so a confidently wrong action is exactly the one that is never flagged.

questions.question: A social services department is asked how it will demonstrate that its benefits-eligibility assistant treats applicants fairly. The team's position is that fairness is a property of the underlying model and therefore the provider's responsibility. What is wrong with that position?

options.A: Nothing — fairness originates in training data, which the department has no ability to influence
options.B: Unequal outcomes arise at points the department itself controls — the corpus, prompt framing, examples and routing — so fairness has to be instrumented locally, with every decision logged so that an explanation can be reconstructed
options.C: The department should require a fairness certification from the provider before the assistant is deployed
options.D: The department should publish the model's technical specification so that applicants can assess it for themselves

rationale.correct: Fairness is instrumented rather than assumed, and the points where unequal outcomes actually arise are ones the department owns: which documents form the corpus, how the prompt frames an applicant, which examples anchor the behaviour, and how requests are routed. Treating it as the provider's property leaves every one of those unmonitored. Logging each decision is the other half, because an explanation that cannot be reconstructed cannot reliably be given — and this is a domain where applicants are entitled to one.

distractors.A: Training data is one contributor among several, and it is the only one the department cannot touch. Accepting it as the whole explanation converts a set of controllable choices into an excuse.
distractors.C: A certificate about the model in general says nothing about how this department's corpus, framing and routing combine on its own applicant population, which is where the disparity would arise.
distractors.D: A technical specification is not something an applicant can act on, and transparency about the model's construction is a different obligation from evidence that decisions were made fairly.

questions.question: A staffing agency's CV-screening assistant is found to score candidates from certain postcodes systematically lower than others. Names, ages and demographic fields had already been excluded from its input. What does this outcome most likely indicate, and what should follow?

options.A: The assistant is functioning as designed, since no protected attribute was supplied to it
options.B: Proxy variables such as postcode can encode protected characteristics, so the response is structured bias evaluation across demographic slices, remediation of what it finds, and ongoing fairness monitoring
options.C: The base model's training data is responsible and nothing can be addressed at the application layer
options.D: Scores should be withheld from recruiters so that the disparity cannot influence their decisions

rationale.correct: Removing explicit attributes removes the label, not the signal. Postcode correlates with characteristics the agency is not permitted to select on, and so do school, employment gaps and several other fields that look neutral individually. Because the disparity is only visible in aggregate, finding it requires evaluating outcomes across demographic slices deliberately, and keeping it found requires that evaluation to run continuously rather than once.

distractors.A: This mistakes formal compliance for fairness. The exclusion of protected fields is a necessary step that the observed outcome has already demonstrated to be insufficient.
distractors.C: The agency chose the corpus, the framing and the scoring criteria, all of which shape the outcome. Attributing the disparity entirely upstream abandons the levers it actually holds.
distractors.D: Hiding the score conceals the evidence of the disparity while the disparity continues to shape which candidates progress. It removes the ability to detect the harm rather than the harm.

questions.question: A telehealth provider sends complete consultation transcripts, including patient names and contact details, to a third-party quality-analytics platform hosted in another jurisdiction. The data protection officer raises an objection. Which architectural change most directly addresses it?

options.A: Add a clause to the privacy notice stating that consultations may be analysed for quality purposes
options.B: Apply data minimisation: redact or pseudonymise personal data before it leaves the system boundary, retaining only what the monitoring purpose actually requires
options.C: Encrypt the transcripts in transit to the analytics platform
options.D: Reduce the retention period the analytics platform applies to the transcripts it holds

rationale.correct: The objection is that more personal data is crossing a boundary than the purpose requires. Quality monitoring examines how a consultation was conducted, which does not depend on knowing whose consultation it was, so redaction or pseudonymisation before the transcript leaves the system boundary preserves the entire analytical value while removing the exposure. That is data minimisation applied architecturally rather than promised procedurally.

distractors.A: A privacy notice provides notice. It does not reduce what is transferred, and disclosure of an excessive transfer does not make the transfer proportionate.
distractors.C: Encryption in transit protects the data between the two systems and leaves it fully identifiable at the destination, which is where the objection is directed.
distractors.D: A shorter retention period shortens the exposure without reducing it. The identifiable transcripts still cross the jurisdiction boundary and are still processed there.

questions.question: A wealth manager wants an assistant that answers adviser questions using client portfolio records. Several design questions are open. Which one must be settled at the architecture stage rather than treated as a post-launch improvement?

options.A: Whether the assistant cites the source record behind each figure it quotes
options.B: Whether every component in the data path — the model, retrieval, logging and any subprocessor — meets the applicable obligations, with the agreements in place before client data flows through any of them
options.C: Which adoption metrics will be reported to the board once advisers are using it
options.D: Whether advisers can export the assistant's answers into client-facing reports

rationale.correct: The obligations attached to client financial data determine what the architecture is permitted to be — which services may touch the data, under what agreements, with what logging and in which jurisdiction. Every one of those is expensive to change once built and impossible to change retrospectively for data that has already flowed, because the transfer has occurred. Settling it first is what makes the rest of the design lawful; discovering it afterwards is a breach rather than a backlog item.

distractors.A: Source citation is a genuine improvement to adviser trust and can be added to a working assistant without disturbing its architecture, which is what makes it a post-launch candidate rather than a gate.
distractors.C: Adoption metrics report on the deployment after it exists. They are worth agreeing early and nothing about the architecture depends on them.
distractors.D: Export into client-facing reports raises real questions about review and accuracy, and it is a capability that can be added later once the underlying data path is sound.

questions.question: A charity's fundraising assistant falls under a donor-data regulation. The compliance lead has listed each of the regulation's requirements and mapped every one to a paragraph in the architecture document. An external audit is due. Which TWO things are missing? (Select TWO)

options.A: A named owner for each control, so that responsibility for it sits with a person rather than with a document
options.B: A living evidence artifact for each control, revalidated over time, because an auditor accepts proof that a control is operating rather than a description of it
options.C: A legal opinion confirming that the regulation applies to the charity in the first place
options.D: A summary of the regulation circulated to everyone working in fundraising
options.E: A copy of the architecture document lodged with the regulator in advance of the audit

rationale.correct: A regulation states an outcome and leaves the charity to choose the control, so the chain has to run from obligation to a specific control, to a named owner, to a living evidence artifact. The mapping stops at the control, which means every one of them currently has no one accountable for it and nothing showing it is operating. A control with no owner and no evidence goes quietly non-operational over time and fails at exactly this moment, because what a reviewer accepts is proof the control is live rather than the control's description.

distractors.C: Applicability is a reasonable thing to confirm and the charity has already proceeded on the basis that it applies. Reopening it now defers the work rather than completing it, and an opinion changes nothing about whether the controls operate.
distractors.D: Circulating a summary raises awareness among staff. Awareness is not a control, has no owner, and produces no artefact an auditor can examine.
distractors.E: Lodging the document shares the description that already exists. It supplies the regulator with the same thing the charity has, which is an account of intent rather than evidence of operation.

questions.question: For each activity, identify the lifecycle phase it primarily belongs to. Options may be used more than once.

scenarios.text: Interviewing frontline staff to understand how quotations are produced today and where the time goes.
Selecting the retrieval strategy and defining the guardrail architecture for the agreed use case.
Walking the client's engineers through the runbooks and transferring operational ownership to them.
Reviewing production evaluation trends and prioritising the next round of prompt improvements.
Facilitating a workshop to agree what success will mean and how it will be measured.

rationale.correct: The first and last both belong to structured discovery, which runs as a four-category process: understanding how the work is done today and agreeing what success will mean are two of those categories, and neither is a design activity even though both shape the design. Choosing the retrieval strategy and the guardrail architecture is design, because it makes architectural commitments against requirements that have already been agreed. Transferring operational ownership with the runbooks is handoff, the point at which the receiving team becomes able to run the system without its builders. Reviewing production evaluation trends to prioritise the next improvements is monitoring and iteration, which is the only phase that uses evidence from real running to decide what happens next.

questions.question: During discovery for a regional railway's incident-reporting assistant, an operations manager says the team would really like it to feel fast. The architect notes this down in the manager's own words and moves on. What should have happened instead?

options.A: Recording it verbatim is correct, since discovery exists to capture what stakeholders actually say
options.B: The remark should be set aside, because a feeling is not something a requirement can be written against
options.C: The preference should be translated into a constraint — a stated response-time target with the assumption behind it labelled — and written as a requirement row the design can be traced to
options.D: The remark should be passed to the sponsor to decide how it ranks against the other requests

rationale.correct: Discovery translates every preference into a constraint, because a preference cannot be designed against, tested against or traced to. Turning wanting it to feel fast into a response-time target with its assumption labelled makes it something the architecture can be built to satisfy and the evaluation can confirm. Labelling the assumption matters as much as the number: it records that the target came from an interpretation of a stated preference, so it can be revisited if the interpretation was wrong.

distractors.A: A faithful transcript preserves ambiguity rather than resolving it. Everyone reading the requirement later supplies their own number, and the disagreement surfaces during acceptance instead of during discovery.
distractors.B: Setting it aside discards a real requirement because it arrived in imprecise language, which is how systems come to be technically correct and rejected by the people who asked for them.
distractors.D: Prioritisation is a legitimate question and it cannot be answered while the item is still a feeling. The sponsor would be ranking something nobody has defined.

questions.question: A professional services firm is concluding discovery for a new engagement. Which TWO outputs are most important to have documented before design begins? (Select TWO)

options.A: Agreed, measurable success criteria with acceptance thresholds tied to the business problem
options.B: An assessment of data availability, data quality, access constraints and compliance obligations
options.C: A working prototype the sponsor can try, so the conversation has something concrete in front of it
options.D: The model version that will be pinned in production
options.E: A signed statement of work fixing the delivery date

rationale.correct: Design decisions hang off two anchors and neither can be inferred later. Measurable success criteria with agreed acceptance thresholds define what the system has to achieve, which is what every subsequent trade-off is resolved against. The data assessment defines what the design is permitted and able to do — what exists, whether it is good enough, who may see it and under what obligations. Design that begins without the first has no target; design that begins without the second gets rebuilt.

distractors.C: A prototype anchors the discussion on one particular solution before the problem has been agreed, and it tends to convert a design conversation into a critique of the prototype.
distractors.D: The model version is a build decision. Fixing it at the end of discovery commits to an implementation detail before the requirements that would inform it exist.
distractors.E: A fixed delivery date is a commercial commitment made before anyone knows what is being built or whether the data supports it, which is how a scope is agreed that cannot be delivered.

questions.question: An agency asks whether automated permit assessment is feasible. Testing shows the assistant handles standard applications reliably but cannot assess applications involving heritage-listed sites, which are a meaningful share of the caseload. How should the architect state the verdict?

options.A: Feasible as scoped, with heritage applications handled by the assistant and simply reviewed more carefully than the rest
options.B: Not feasible, since a substantial share of the caseload falls outside what the assistant can assess
options.C: Feasible with constraints, documenting the load-bearing boundary condition — heritage-listed applications route to human assessment — so the limit is explicit and can be revisited
options.D: Defer the verdict until the heritage cases can be made to work, so a single clean answer can be given

rationale.correct: The verdict is stated in one of three forms, and this case is squarely the middle one. Feasible with constraints is honest about both halves of the finding, and the load-bearing boundary condition is what makes it actionable: it names the specific limit the feasibility rests on, so the agency knows what it is accepting and what would have to change for the scope to widen. A documented boundary is also what allows the decision to be revisited without reopening the whole assessment.

distractors.A: Declaring it feasible as scoped while quietly relying on more careful review is the verdict that causes trouble later, because the constraint is real and is now unrecorded. Nobody downstream knows which applications the assistant should not have been trusted with.
distractors.B: Not feasible discards a capability that demonstrably works for the majority of the caseload. It answers a question about the whole when the finding is about a nameable part.
distractors.D: The purpose of the verdict is to inform a decision now. Deferring until every case works withholds a usable answer in order to produce a simpler one later.

questions.question: During discovery, a retail bank's executive sponsor states that the assistant must be 100% accurate before it can launch. What is the most effective response from the architect?

options.A: Agree to the requirement and add further testing phases until measured accuracy reaches 100%
options.B: Decline the engagement, since the requirement as stated cannot be satisfied
options.C: Explain that these systems are probabilistic, then work with the sponsor to define measurable acceptance criteria and an error-handling strategy proportionate to the business risk
options.D: Propose a smaller and more tightly constrained model so that there is less scope for error

rationale.correct: The sponsor is expressing a legitimate concern in a form that cannot be delivered, and the architect's job is to convert it into something that can. Naming the probabilistic nature of the system is the first half; the second is agreeing what accuracy is sufficient for this decision and what happens when the system is wrong. An error-handling strategy proportionate to business risk is usually what the sponsor was actually asking for, since the real worry is consequences rather than percentages.

distractors.A: Agreeing to a target that cannot be reached commits the project to failing its own acceptance criteria, and the testing phases consume budget without ever closing.
distractors.B: This treats a conversation as an impasse. The requirement is a first statement of a concern rather than a final position, and it is the kind of position that moves once the trade-off is made concrete.
distractors.D: A more constrained model changes the error rate somewhat and does nothing about the expectation, which remains at an unreachable absolute. It answers a question the sponsor did not ask.

questions.question: A waste management company's finance director instructs the team to use the cheapest available model for a routing assistant whose output feeds regulatory emissions reporting. Internal testing shows the cheapest tier has a materially higher error rate on this task. What is the architect's most professional course of action?

options.A: Comply with the instruction and record the concern in the project risk register so that it is documented
options.B: Present the trade-off in three elements including the reversal cost — error rate, downstream rework and regulatory exposure set against the saving — recommend a position, and let the accountable stakeholder decide with full information
options.C: Use the more capable model and absorb the difference elsewhere in the budget so the reporting stays sound
options.D: Escalate above the finance director to the audit committee, given the regulatory exposure involved

rationale.correct: The finance director is entitled to make this call and is currently making it without the information that would change it. Presenting the trade-off in three elements, including what it would cost to reverse the decision once emissions reports have been filed on the cheaper tier, converts a cost instruction into an informed choice. The architect recommends and the accountable stakeholder decides, which is what keeps both the decision and the relationship sound.

distractors.A: The risk register records that somebody knew. It does not put the information in front of the person making the decision, which is the one thing that would let them make it differently.
distractors.C: Quietly overriding an instruction removes the decision from the person accountable for it, and concealing the budget movement compounds a technical disagreement into a question of trust.
distractors.D: Escalation may become appropriate and it is premature before the trade-off has been put to the finance director at all. Going over someone's head on a conversation that has not happened damages the relationship the work depends on.

questions.question: A theatre group's commercial director requires sub-second complete responses from an assistant that performs multi-step retrieval and reasoning over the booking system. Engineering analysis shows the pipeline cannot complete in under three seconds. Which approach best manages this expectation?

options.A: Accept the sub-second requirement and expect optimisation work to close the gap before launch
options.B: Remove the retrieval and reasoning steps so that the stated target becomes achievable
options.C: Present the latency breakdown, negotiate an SLA the pipeline can actually honour, and propose streaming and progress indicators so the experience feels responsive within it
options.D: Commit to sub-second responses for demonstrations, and explain the production difference once the system is live

rationale.correct: Expectation management is grounded in what the pipeline can actually do, and the latency breakdown is what makes that concrete rather than a matter of opinion. Negotiating an SLA the system can honour protects both parties, and streaming with progress indication addresses the underlying concern, which is almost always that the assistant should not feel unresponsive rather than that a specific figure must be met. Perceived speed and total completion time are separable, and this is the case where separating them resolves the disagreement.

distractors.A: Signing up to a target the analysis says is unreachable defers the conversation to a point where the commitment is public and the disappointment is larger.
distractors.B: Removing retrieval and reasoning meets the number by deleting the capability that justified building the assistant, which trades the requirement for the purpose.
distractors.D: A demonstration tuned to a figure the production system cannot meet guarantees the gap surfaces after launch, and it surfaces as a broken promise rather than as an engineering constraint.

questions.question: A hospital trust's clinical documentation assistant has been live for a quarter. The team has dashboards and alerting, but when a metric moves nobody is certain what is supposed to happen next. Which TWO measures close that gap? (Select TWO)

options.A: A decision layer that maps each signal to a trigger action and to a named owner who acts on it
options.B: SLA thresholds set from their real sources — the clinical service standard and the supplier contract — rather than chosen to sit just above current performance
options.C: More granular dashboards, broken down by ward and by document type
options.D: A weekly meeting at which the team reviews whatever the dashboards happened to show
options.E: Alerting on every available metric, so that nothing can go unnoticed

rationale.correct: The trust has built the observing half of a feedback loop and none of the deciding half: it has signals and no decisions. Mapping each signal to a trigger action and a named owner is what turns a moving metric into something that happens, and naming owners is the part that stops a shared responsibility from being nobody's. Setting the thresholds from their real sources is what makes the trigger meaningful, because a threshold derived from current performance only ever fires when things get worse than they happen to be today rather than worse than the service requires.

distractors.C: Finer breakdowns produce a more precise description of a situation nobody knows how to respond to. The gap is in the decision layer rather than in the resolution of the observation.
distractors.D: A standing review looks at whatever is visible on the day and depends on somebody noticing. It is a detective habit rather than a defined trigger, and it operates on a weekly cycle regardless of urgency.
distractors.E: Alerting on everything is how alerting stops working. The volume trains the team to dismiss alerts, so the signal that mattered arrives among a hundred that did not.

questions.question: Two months after launch, a football club's sponsor is visibly losing interest in its supporter-services assistant. The fortnightly report shows token spend, latency and uptime and nothing else. Which change would most improve stakeholder alignment?

options.A: Add further technical metrics so that the report is more thorough and complete
options.B: Increase the reporting frequency from fortnightly to weekly so momentum is maintained
options.C: Report against the business success criteria agreed at discovery — staff hours saved, enquiry resolution rate — with the technical metrics as supporting detail, using a translation layer that maps one to the other
options.D: Replace the report with an open dashboard the sponsor can consult whenever they wish

rationale.correct: The sponsor funded a business outcome and is being shown operating statistics, so the report never answers the question they are actually asking. Leading with the success criteria agreed at discovery closes that loop, and the translation layer is what makes the technical metrics useful rather than discarded — latency becomes the reason resolution times moved, spend becomes the cost side of hours saved. That mapping is what sustains sponsorship into a second phase.

distractors.A: More of the content the sponsor is already not engaging with makes the report longer without making it relevant, and thoroughness in the wrong dimension reads as a team talking to itself.
distractors.B: Doubling the frequency of a report that does not answer the sponsor's question doubles the reminder that it does not. Cadence is not the problem.
distractors.D: An open dashboard transfers the work of interpretation to the sponsor, who lacks the context to map operating metrics onto the outcomes they care about and will simply stop opening it.

questions.question: A consultancy is handing a completed solution to the client's internal engineering team, who will own and evolve it from here. Beyond the code itself, which artefact set matters most to a successful handoff?

options.A: The full history of prompt drafts explored during development, so the team can see what was tried
options.B: Architecture decision records explaining the key trade-offs and the alternatives that were rejected, operational runbooks, and evaluation baselines the team can re-run
options.C: Direct access to the consultancy's engineers for six months of follow-up questions
options.D: A prioritised backlog of the features that were considered but not built

rationale.correct: The receiving team needs to do three things: understand why the system is the way it is, keep it running, and change it safely. Decision records with the rejected alternatives answer the first and prevent the new team from re-litigating settled questions or reintroducing an option that was already ruled out. Runbooks answer the second. Re-runnable evaluation baselines answer the third, because they let the team verify that a change has not broken anything without having to have been present for the original build.

distractors.A: The draft history is a record of the journey rather than a tool for ownership. It shows what was tried without recording what was concluded, which is the part that transfers.
distractors.C: Access to the original engineers is genuinely useful and it substitutes for the artefacts rather than supplementing them. It also expires, at which point the team is where it started, and it leaves them dependent for the familiar problems rather than only the new ones.
distractors.D: An unbuilt-features backlog describes work that does not exist. The team needs to operate what does.

questions.question: An insurance broker's first assistant has been live for two quarters and the sponsor is considering funding a second project. Which TWO belong in the outcome document that justifies that expansion? (Select TWO)

options.A: The before metric captured prior to launch, so the improvement can be stated as a comparison rather than as an assertion
options.B: The reuse note recording which components, patterns and controls the next project can inherit
options.C: A list of every prompt revision made during the build
options.D: The number of requests the assistant has served since it went live
options.E: A statement that the project completed on schedule and within its budget

rationale.correct: An outcome document exists to justify the next investment, which takes two things. The before metric turns the claimed improvement into a comparison somebody can check, and it can only be captured before launch, which is why it has to have been planned for. The reuse note is what makes the second project cheaper than the first, by recording which components, patterns and control register entries carry over rather than being rediscovered. Together they answer what this delivered and what the next one starts with.

distractors.C: The revision history documents how the build proceeded. It supports no claim about what the assistant achieved and nothing in it transfers to the next project.
distractors.D: Request volume shows the assistant was used. It cannot distinguish heavy use that saved time from heavy use caused by answers that needed asking twice.
distractors.E: Delivering on schedule and on budget is a credit to the delivery and says nothing about whether the outcome was worth having, which is the question the sponsor is weighing.

questions.question: Midway through building a film production company's scheduling assistant, stakeholders keep adding requests: new data sources, further user groups, additional output formats. Which practice best manages this while preserving the working relationship?

options.A: Absorb the requests without comment, since accommodating stakeholders is what keeps them engaged
options.B: Decline all changes until the originally agreed scope has shipped
options.C: Assess each request against the agreed success criteria and scope baseline, make the impact visible before accepting it, and re-baseline timeline, cost and risk with sponsor sign-off when accepted changes materially alter the plan
options.D: Add every request to a second-phase backlog without assessing whether any of them belong in this one

rationale.correct: Healthy change management makes each request's impact visible against the agreed baseline before it is accepted, so the stakeholder chooses the change knowing what it costs rather than discovering it in a slipped date. Formally re-baselining when accepted changes move the plan is the other half: it keeps the plan an honest description of what will happen. The relationship survives scope change because nothing about it is hidden, not because the changes are refused or silently absorbed.

distractors.A: Silent absorption erodes the schedule invisibly until the delay arrives with no explanation attached to it, at which point the stakeholders who made the requests experience it as the team missing its commitments.
distractors.B: A blanket refusal protects the plan and spends the relationship, and some of these requests may be genuinely important discoveries rather than scope creep. The assessment is what distinguishes them.
distractors.D: Deferring everything unexamined is a refusal with a more agreeable form of words. A request that materially affects the design is cheapest to accommodate now and most expensive after the build has assumed it away.

questions.question: A games studio has rolled AI-assisted coding tools out across its engineering team. Early adopters each configured their tooling differently, and the result is inconsistent code style and several engineers solving the same problems separately. What is the most effective enablement step?

options.A: Let each engineer keep their own configuration, since productivity tooling is a personal matter
options.B: Establish a shared, version-controlled baseline of project configuration and standards that every engineer's tooling inherits, reserving personal configuration for genuine individual preference
options.C: Restrict the tooling to the most senior engineers until sensible conventions have emerged
options.D: Adopt whichever configuration the most productive engineer uses and roll it out across the studio

rationale.correct: Team-scale productivity comes from a shared baseline held in version control, so that every engineer inherits proven practice by default and improvements propagate rather than staying with whoever discovered them. Keeping a personal layer on top matters too: consistency is needed where the output is shared, and imposing it on genuine preference generates resistance for no benefit. Consistency where it counts, freedom where it does not.

distractors.A: This describes the situation the studio already has. Configuration genuinely is personal in places, and code style and reusable workflows are not, which is exactly the distinction the current arrangement fails to make.
distractors.C: Restricting access reduces the inconsistency by reducing the adoption the rollout exists to create, and conventions do not emerge from a smaller group any more reliably than from a larger one.
distractors.D: One engineer's configuration is tuned to one engineer's work and one engineer's habits. Their productivity is evidence that it suits them, not that it generalises.

questions.question: A government digital service is standing up AI tooling across several delivery teams at once. Which TWO decisions belong in the team setup, taken up front rather than settled as they arise? (Select TWO)

options.A: How Skills will be distributed by scope — org-provisioned for everyone, plugins for group and organisation targeting with versioned updates and rollback, project Skills for a single team, API Skills for programmatic reuse
options.B: Model and budget guardrails bounding what each team is able to consume
options.C: Which development environment each team will standardise on
options.D: A backlog of the Skills to be written during the first quarter
options.E: Which delivery team will pilot the tooling first

rationale.correct: Team setup is shared configuration, a distribution approach and a spend posture, all decided up front because all three are expensive to impose retrospectively. Choosing how Skills are distributed by scope determines who can publish what to whom and how a bad version is rolled back, which is not something to work out after several teams have published conflicting Skills. Model and budget guardrails set the consumption boundary before consumption starts, which is the only point at which it can be set without taking something away.

distractors.C: Editor choice is largely personal and can differ per team without affecting anyone else, provided the shared configuration is inherited regardless of which environment reads it.
distractors.D: A Skills backlog is content produced within the structure. Writing it before the distribution model exists means deciding what to build without knowing who will be able to use it.
distractors.E: Pilot sequencing is an adoption question and a good one. It is answered after the setup exists, because piloting without guardrails is what the guardrails are meant to prevent.

questions.question: A health technology company gave every engineer access to AI coding tooling two quarters ago. Usage analytics show most engineers treat it as a chat window for occasional questions, while a small number have built it into their workflow and are shipping noticeably faster. What does this pattern indicate?

options.A: The tooling suits some working styles and not others, so usage is best left to individual preference
options.B: Access without enablement stalls at basic chat: adoption has to be engineered through a champion per team who proves the workflow, rolled out in batches so the gain standardises rather than staying with a few individuals
options.C: The high adopters should be moved into a central team that does this work on behalf of everyone else
options.D: Licences should be withdrawn from the engineers who are not using the tooling fully, to concentrate the spend

rationale.correct: This is the signature of access granted without enablement. Handing over a licence gets an engineer as far as asking occasional questions, and the workflow changes that produce the real gain have to be demonstrated by someone doing the same job. A champion per team proves the workflow in context and seeds it locally, and batching the rollout is what turns a few fast individuals into a standardised gain rather than a permanent gap between them and everyone else.

distractors.A: Working style is a real factor and it does not explain a distribution this lopsided. Treating the outcome as preference makes the current state permanent and forgoes the measured gain the small group has already demonstrated.
distractors.C: Centralising the adopters creates a queue in front of the capability and removes the people best placed to demonstrate the workflow from the teams that most need to see it.
distractors.D: Withdrawing licences punishes engineers for an enablement failure that was not theirs, and it removes the access that is the precondition for the adoption the company wants.

questions.question: An engineering organisation has adopted AI-assisted development. A retrospective finds that AI-authored pull requests are merged roughly three times faster than human-authored ones and are approved with markedly fewer review comments, yet AI-authored changes account for a disproportionate share of production incidents. Which interpretation best fits this evidence?

options.A: The tooling produces lower-quality code than human authors and its use should be restricted to non-production repositories
options.B: Reviewers are extending unwarranted trust to changes that arrive fluent, well-formatted and confidently explained, so review is least rigorous exactly where its scrutiny is most needed
options.C: The incident figures are confounded by AI-authored changes being more numerous, and no action is warranted until the volumes are normalised
options.D: Requiring a second reviewer on every AI-authored change would resolve the discrepancy

rationale.correct: The evidence is about the review step rather than the authoring step. Faster merges with fewer comments is a measurement of reviewer behaviour, and it points at fluency being read as correctness — well-structured code with a confident explanation suppresses the scepticism that finds defects. Holding AI-generated code to correctness, security and maintainability means the review is genuinely performed: independent of the authoring context, with the author able to explain what shipped, captured as a verification checklist that gates before production.

distractors.A: The data cannot isolate authoring quality, because these changes never received comparable scrutiny. Restricting the tooling forfeits its benefit without testing the explanation the evidence actually supports.
distractors.C: Normalising for volume is a sound analytical instinct, and merge time and comment rate are already per-change measures that volume does not explain. Treating the whole finding as a counting artefact discards the part that is not.
distractors.D: Adding a reviewer multiplies a process that is demonstrably not applying scrutiny. Two reviewers extending the same unwarranted trust find no more than one did.

questions.question: A financial technology platform team wants to scale AI-assisted development across the organisation without introducing operational risk. Which TWO practices best support that goal? (Select TWO)

options.A: Constrain what automated tooling is permitted to execute — allowed commands, protected branches, approval gates for destructive actions
options.B: Maintain shared configuration, prompt standards and reusable workflows in version control so that teams inherit proven practice
options.C: Give the tooling unrestricted credentials so that friction does not slow adoption down
options.D: Prohibit engineers from editing generated code, so that its provenance stays unambiguous
options.E: Adopt each new AI development tool as it is released, so the organisation stays current

rationale.correct: Scaling safely needs an accelerator and a brake, and these are one of each. Shared standards in version control spread proven practice, so growth in adoption is growth in consistent adoption rather than in divergence. Execution constraints bound what automation can do wrong: allowed commands, protected branches and approval gates for destructive actions mean the blast radius stays fixed as the number of engineers using the tooling rises.

distractors.C: Unrestricted credentials maximise the blast radius at precisely the moment the number of automated actors is increasing, which is the opposite of scaling without operational risk.
distractors.D: Prohibiting engineers from editing generated code removes the human judgement that makes the output trustworthy and leaves them shipping code they were not permitted to improve.
distractors.E: Immediate adoption of every release means continuous churn in the shared baseline, and each new tool arrives unvetted into an environment the team is trying to keep predictable.

questions.question: A retailer's production agent has begun taking unexpected actions on a subset of requests. The on-call engineer's instinct is to rewrite the system prompt immediately. What should happen first?

options.A: Rewrite the system prompt, since prompt defects are the most common cause of unexpected agent behaviour
options.B: Inspect traces of the affected sessions — inputs, retrieved context, tool calls and outputs — to connect the symptoms to their architecture cause before changing anything
options.C: Roll back to the model version the agent ran on two quarters ago as a precaution
options.D: Disable the agent and return the workload to manual handling until the cause is known

rationale.correct: Operational support means connecting symptoms to architecture causes rather than treating the symptom, and traces of the affected sessions are where that connection is made. They show whether the behaviour originates in the inputs, the retrieved context, a tool returning something unexpected, or the prompt — four causes with four different remedies. Diagnosing first also produces the material for the runbooks and escalation paths that let the team handle the next occurrence without needing help.

distractors.A: Rewriting the prompt before diagnosis is a guess that changes the component most likely to be working. If the cause lies in retrieval or a tool, the rewrite masks the signal while destabilising behaviour that was previously correct.
distractors.C: Rolling back two quarters is a large intervention with no evidence connecting it to the cause, and it reverses every improvement since then to address a fault that may have nothing to do with the model version.
distractors.D: Withdrawing the agent entirely responds to a subset failure by removing the whole capability, and it does so before anyone knows whether the cause is narrow and quickly fixed.
